**"Companion firmware" Compile/Flash card built on Configuration → POCSAG, 2026-07-30 (same day, right after the arduino-cli toolchain was proven live from the CLI).** Turns the manual `arduino-cli compile`/`upload` commands just tested by hand into a real dashboard feature. User's original ask: a card between "POCSAG companions" and "DAPNET settings" with Compile + Flash buttons, port taken from the configured companion (ask which one only if multiple are configured), streamed compile output shown somewhere but collapsible/hidden by default. Also specifically asked for the board list to be a pulldown auto-populated by reading the `.ino`'s own board defines, rather than hardcoded, since "we can build ttgo and heltec for now."

**Backend** (`src/api/routes/pocsag_firmware_routes.py`, new file):
- `GET /api/pocsag/firmware/targets` -- scans `pocsag_companion.ino` for every `#define BOARD_*`/`//#define BOARD_*` line (regex `_BOARD_DEFINE_RE`, scoped to the `BOARD_` prefix so it never touches the sketch's many other unrelated `#define`s) and cross-references against `_KNOWN_BOARDS` (macro -> label/fqbn -- the one piece that can't be auto-derived, since a board's FQBN isn't spelled out in the source). A third board added to the sketch later shows up in the pulldown automatically; still needs one line added to `_KNOWN_BOARDS` before it's actually buildable.
- `POST /api/pocsag/firmware/compile/stream` -- `_select_board_define(macro)` rewrites the sketch's two toggle lines (uncomment target, comment every other known macro) before running `arduino-cli --config-file /opt/arduino-cli/arduino-cli.yaml compile --fqbn <fqbn> <sketch_dir>` via `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec`, streamed line-by-line as NDJSON through `_stream_subprocess()` (new small helper, same wire shape as `src/api/update/streaming.py`'s `stream_update()` -- `{"type":"started","cmd":[...]}`, `{"type":"line","stream":"stdout"|"stderr","text":...}` per line, final `{"type":"result","result":{"returncode":...,"success":...}}`, the nested `"result"` key deliberately matching `UpdateStreamClient.postNdjson`'s own expected shape so the same frontend client class works unmodified).
- `POST /api/pocsag/firmware/flash/stream` -- resolves the target port SERVER-SIDE from `config.capture.pocsag_serial` by label (never trusts a raw path from the browser), then -- new safety behavior, not just a straight upload -- if that device's `DapnetSerialSource` is currently connected, calls `await source.stop()` before flashing (esptool needs exclusive access to reset+write the board) and `await source.start()` after a 3s settle delay, reporting whether it actually reconnected. This directly closes the gap hit earlier the same day (reflashing left DAPNET capture dead until a manual `systemctl restart meshpoint`) for flashes done through this new feature specifically -- flashes done by hand outside Meshpoint still hit that gap, unchanged.
- Wired into `src/api/server.py`: import, `app.include_router(pocsag_firmware_routes.router, dependencies=protected)`, `pocsag_firmware_routes.init_routes(config=config, dapnet_sources=_find_dapnet_sources(coord))`.

**Frontend** (`frontend/js/configuration/pocsag_serial_card.js`, extended, no new file -- matches the existing one-class/multiple-cards pattern already used for "POCSAG companions"/"DAPNET settings"): new `<article class="cfg-card">` inserted between the two existing ones. Board `<select>` populated on mount from `/targets`; device `<select>` populated in `render()` from the same `config.capture.pocsag_serial` list the existing device rows already use, hidden entirely when 0 or 1 devices are configured (skips the picker when there's nothing to choose between, per the user's own suggestion). Compile has a `window.confirmModal` guard on Flash only (compile is non-destructive; flash briefly interrupts capture and writes real flash). Both actions share `_runFirmwareStream()`, calling `window.UpdateStreamClient.postNdjson()` (same NDJSON client Settings → Updates already uses, reused as-is -- no new client class needed) into a `<pre class="cfg-firmware-output">` panel, hidden by default with a "Show/Hide output" toggle button; auto-reveals itself on failure. New CSS `.cfg-firmware-output` in `configuration.css`, matching `settings.css`'s `.update-progress__terminal-body` look (same monospace dark panel) but standalone rather than nested in a bigger terminal wrapper.

**Design decision, explicitly discussed with the user first**: the sketch's board target is a source-level `#define`, not an `arduino-cli` build flag -- there's no way to say "compile for TTGO" without editing the file first. Went with the pragmatic fix (`_select_board_define` sed-toggles the two lines server-side before every compile) rather than the cleaner refactor (board selected via a `--build-property` instead of mutating source), per the user's explicit "for now" framing. **This means every Compile run mutates the checked-out `pocsag_companion.ino` on disk** (leaves it in whichever board's state was last compiled) -- expected/by design, not a bug, matching exactly what was done by hand earlier this session; worth remembering if `git status` ever shows this file dirty on the Pi.

**Verification (Mac, stub-based per this repo's testing constraints)**: `ast.parse` clean; `node --check` clean; board-discovery/select-define round-tripped against the REAL `.ino` file (select TTGO -> select Heltec back -> byte-identical to git HEAD, confirmed via `git status --short` staying clean); both streaming routes exercised end-to-end with stubbed `fastapi`/`pydantic`/audit/auth and a fake subprocess command (`true`)/fake `DapnetSerialSource`, confirming: the NDJSON event shape, the stop-before/start-after behavior around a connected source, and the 400 rejection for an unconfigured device label; `tests/test_html_assets.py` 7/7; changelog re-parses (26 sections). **LIVE-VERIFIED through the actual browser UI, same day**: Compile ran against the real Heltec V3 (Sketch uses 1,210,511 bytes/36%). Two bugs found and fixed from this first live click-through:
- Compile's arduino-cli invocation was missing `-v` -- the whole ~10s+ build produced zero output until the final size summary, making the panel look frozen the entire time despite working correctly. Added `-v` to the compile command.
- The "Companion to flash" picker showed up even with only one companion configured (should auto-select and stay hidden) -- `.cfg-field`'s own `display: flex` was silently beating the browser's `[hidden] { display: none }` rule, same bug class as the earlier LoRaWAN search-box fix (`.lw-search-wrap[hidden]`). Fixed with an explicit `.cfg-field[hidden] { display: none; }` override in configuration.css.

Flash then verified fully working end-to-end for real: released `/dev/serial/by-path/...-usb-0:1.3:1.0-port0` (the STABLE by-path entry, not a raw ttyUSBN -- confirms the earlier renumbering concern doesn't apply here since the configured device already uses by-path), ran esptool's full write+verify+reset, waited 3s, and `dapnet_heltec reconnected` on the same by-path port automatically -- no manual `systemctl restart meshpoint` needed. This closes the loop on the "flash leaves capture dead" gap for any flash done through this new button specifically.

**New feature: "Meshtastic firmware" flash card on Configuration → Serial, 2026-07-30 (same day, right after the POCSAG compile/flash card).** User's plan: the Heltec V3 that was running `pocsag_companion`/DAPNET is done with that duty (POCSAG capture source disabled in config) — repurpose it into a Meshtastic USB stick instead. Explicitly a SEPARATE, NEW feature from the POCSAG card, not an extension of it (user: "no its a new thing we want to build, the pocsag/dapnet is done... we want to flash meshtastic, in the correct serial tab").

**Key difference from the POCSAG compile/flash card**: Meshtastic firmware is PlatformIO-built upstream, not an Arduino sketch — no compiling happens here at all, only downloading an official prebuilt release and writing it with `esptool` directly.

**Research done before building** (via WebFetch + the GitHub API + downloading real release assets):
- Confirmed via the official Meshtastic CLI-flashing docs that their own tooling (`device-install.sh`) is itself just an esptool wrapper around a downloaded release ZIP -- no compiling.
- Found real board slugs via `meshtastic/firmware`'s own release manifest (`firmware-<version>.json`, top-level asset, `{"targets": [{"board":"heltec-v3","platform":"esp32s3"}, ...]}`, 129 total targets) -- confirmed `heltec-v3` for the Heltec, and TWO TTGO variants exist (`tlora-v2-1-1_6`, `tlora-v3-3-0-tcxo`) -- user confirmed theirs is `tlora-v2-1-1_6`.
- Downloaded and inspected REAL release zips (`firmware-esp32s3-*.zip`, `firmware-esp32-*.zip`) for both boards: each board ships a `.factory.bin` (combined bootloader+partition-table+app, meant for offset 0x0 -- i.e. a from-scratch flash), a plain `.bin` (app-only, `part_name: app0`, for updating an already-Meshtastic-partitioned board -- NOT used here), a `littlefs-*.bin` (`part_name: spiffs`), and a `.mt.json` metadata file listing every file + `part[]` table with real offsets. Verified the `spiffs` offset differs by board (`0x670000` for Heltec V3/esp32s3, `0x300000` for TTGO/esp32) -- confirms hardcoding offsets per-board would have been wrong; reading them from each release's own `.mt.json` at flash time is required, not just tidy.
- Confirmed exact esptool 5.x CLI syntax by temp-installing it in a scratch pip target dir and checking `--help`: `esptool --chip <mcu> --port <port> --baud <rate> write-flash --erase-all <addr1> <file1> [<addr2> <file2> ...]` (modern subcommand style, not the old `esptool.py write_flash` underscore form). `--erase-all` deliberately used since the board may hold a completely different firmware's partition layout (our exact case).
- Confirmed via `pip3 show -f esptool`'s entry_points that the installed console script is bare `esptool` (not `esptool.py`) -- matches what got added to `install.sh`.

**Also added to `scripts/install.sh`** (user's own request, "i think we also need esptools in the install script"): a bare `esptool` install via `pip3 install --upgrade esptool --break-system-packages`, right after the Meshtastic CLI section. Not redundant with arduino-cli's own bundled `esptool_py` copy -- that one's buried under `/opt/arduino-cli/data/packages/esp32/tools/esptool_py/`, never on `PATH`, and Meshtastic's own official scripts (and this new feature) expect a plain `esptool` command.

**Backend** (`src/api/routes/meshtastic_firmware_routes.py`, new file, mirrors `pocsag_firmware_routes.py`'s NDJSON-streaming shape):
- `GET /api/config/serial/firmware/targets` -- curated board list (`_CURATED_BOARDS`: heltec-v3, tlora-v2-1-1_6, tlora-v3-3-0-tcxo), NOT the full ~130-board Meshtastic catalog (discussed with user first: a plain `<select>` with 130 entries is unwieldy without search, and Meshtastic's own docs specifically warn about picking a wrong-but-similar variant -- exactly the risk a giant list invites; can be expanded later since the backend already fetches the full manifest to resolve chip/platform anyway).
- `_ensure_board_firmware_cached_sync(board)` -- fetches the latest release, resolves the board's chip architecture from the top-level manifest, downloads the matching ZIP to a temp file (not held in memory -- ~170MB per architecture), extracts just the 3 needed files (`.mt.json`, `.factory.bin`, `littlefs-*.bin`) into `<repo_root>/data/meshtastic-firmware/<board>/<version>/` (moved here from a standalone `/opt/meshtastic-firmware` after the permission bug below -- see the follow-up note), and returns the resolved mcu + file paths + littlefs offset (read from the `.mt.json`'s own `part[]` table, matched by name `"spiffs"`). Cache-checked by version dir existing -- a repeat flash of the same board/version skips the whole download+extract, verified taking ~0.2s instead of the full network round-trip.
- `POST /api/config/serial/firmware/flash/stream` -- resolves the port server-side from `config.capture.serial` by label (never trusted from the browser, same discipline as the POCSAG flash route), releases the matching `SerialCaptureSource` if connected (has the same `stop()`/`start()` shape as `DapnetSerialSource`, confirmed by reading `src/capture/serial_source.py`), runs `esptool ... write-flash --erase-all 0x0 <factory.bin> <spiffs_offset> <littlefs.bin>` streamed as NDJSON (duplicated `_stream_subprocess()` helper rather than importing the POCSAG module's copy, since the two routers are otherwise independent), reconnects the source afterward with the same 3s-settle-then-start pattern.
- Wired into `server.py`: import, `include_router`, `init_routes(config=config, serial_sources=_find_serial_sources(coord))`.

**Frontend**: extended `frontend/js/configuration/serial_card.js` (not a new file) with a second `cfg-card`, "Meshtastic firmware" -- board pulldown (curated list from `/targets`), device pulldown (only shown with 2+ configured Serial devices, same convention as POCSAG), Flash button gated behind `window.confirmModal` (explicitly destructive -- `--erase-all` wipes the whole chip, unlike the POCSAG card's non-destructive Compile), and an output panel reusing the SAME `.cfg-firmware-output`/`.cfg-firmware-board-field` CSS classes from the POCSAG card (generalized their doc-comments in `configuration.css` to reflect being shared by both cards now). Streams via the same `window.UpdateStreamClient.postNdjson` client, no new JS class needed.

**Verification (Mac, real network calls, not fully stubbed)**: `ast.parse`/`node --check` clean; `_ensure_board_firmware_cached_sync` exercised for REAL against the live `meshtastic/firmware` GitHub release for BOTH `heltec-v3` (esp32s3, littlefs @ 0x670000, ~2.1MB factory.bin) and `tlora-v2-1-1_6` (esp32, littlefs @ 0x300000) -- confirmed correct mcu/offsets, confirmed the cache-hit path is near-instant on a second call, confirmed an unknown board slug raises cleanly; the full `flash_meshtastic_stream` route exercised end-to-end with a stand-in `esptool` command (`true`) and a fake connected `SerialCaptureSource`, confirming stop-before/start-after behavior and the exact `esptool --chip esp32s3 --port ... --baud 921600 write-flash --erase-all 0x0 <factory> 0x670000 <littlefs>` argument construction; `tests/test_html_assets.py` 7/7; changelog re-parses (26 sections).

**LIVE-VERIFIED on real hardware, same day**: flashed the repurposed Heltec V3 through the actual dashboard card -- factory.bin written at 0x0 (1,351,697 bytes, ~20s), littlefs written at 0x670000 (1,572,864 bytes, ~3s), both hash-verified, hard reset via RTS, status "Flashed." User confirmed Meshtastic's own boot screen showing on the board's LCD. Full loop closes out: research (real release inspection) -> build -> permission bug found and properly fixed (moved to data/) -> live flash succeeded on the first real attempt after that fix.

**Real bug hit on the first live attempt, same day**: `[Errno 13] Permission denied: '/opt/meshtastic-firmware'` -- unlike `/opt/arduino-cli`, this cache dir was never pre-created/chowned in install.sh, and `/opt` itself is root-owned, so `meshpoint` can't create a new directory under it on its own. User unblocked immediately with a manual `sudo mkdir -p /opt/meshtastic-firmware && sudo chown meshpoint:meshpoint /opt/meshtastic-firmware`. First fix attempt added the equivalent `mkdir`/`chown` to install.sh -- but the user then asked the better architectural question: "shouldnt it go in /opt/meshpoint?" Correct instinct, acted on immediately: moved `_CACHE_DIR` to `<repo_root>/data/meshtastic-firmware` (resolved dynamically via `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]`, same technique as `pocsag_firmware_routes.py`'s `_SKETCH_DIR`), since `data/` already exists, is already excluded from install.sh's rsync (an upgrade never touches it), and is already owned by `meshpoint` recursively -- removing the need for any dedicated mkdir/chown step in install.sh at all (deleted the ones just added). General principle worth remembering: anything Meshpoint's own code downloads/generates at runtime belongs under `data/`, not a new standalone `/opt/<name>` path -- reserve a separate `/opt` directory for genuinely independent, reusable toolchains (arduino-cli, the SX1302 HAL, redsea, etc.), not for this project's own working data.

**Configuration → Serial can now set a Meshtastic stick's LoRa region live, 2026-07-30 (same day, right after the Meshtastic flash card went live).** After flashing the repurposed Heltec V3 with official Meshtastic firmware (previous entry), it connected and showed real live readouts (Node ID `!09d406f4`, firmware `2.7.26.54e0d8d`, hardware "Heltec V3") -- but `REGION: UNSET` / `FREQUENCY: --`, Meshtastic's deliberate factory-default safety state: it will not transmit at all until a region is explicitly set. User asked "cant we do it like setting name etc in the webinterface?" -- genuinely yes, and better than the CLI-based plan discussed first.

**Key insight, found by reading the existing code rather than guessing**: `SerialCaptureSource` already holds a live `meshtastic-python` `SerialInterface` (`self._interface`) and already has a `set_owner()` method for renaming (an `AdminMessage` via `Node.setOwner()`) -- the SAME `iface.localNode` object that already reads `localConfig.lora.region` for the readout tile can also WRITE it back, over the SAME already-open connection. No port-release dance needed at all here (unlike flashing) -- this is a live in-band config change, not a from-scratch reflash.

**Verified against real meshtastic-python/protobufs source before implementing, not guessed:**
- Fetched the real `RegionCode` enum from `meshtastic/protobufs`' `config.proto` on GitHub -- confirmed `EU_433` = 2 (matches the "433" label on this device) and 37 total region codes.
- Confirmed `ModemPreset.LONG_FAST = 0` -- explains why the topbar chip already showed "LONGFAST" even with region UNSET (it's the actual protobuf default, unrelated to region).
- Fetched `meshtastic-python`'s real `node.py` source (`Node.writeConfig()`) to confirm the exact call shape (`node.localConfig.lora.region = <int>; node.writeConfig("lora")`) AND, critically, that it's safe to call synchronously without blocking the event loop -- `writeConfig()` only sets `onResponse=self.onAckNak` (which waits) when `self != self.iface.localNode`; for the directly-attached device (always true here) it's unconditionally `onResponse=None`, the exact same code path `set_owner()` already relies on and already has a comment explaining (a past bug: an earlier version of `set_owner()` DID call `waitForAckNak()` and froze the whole dashboard for 20s on every rename, since nothing was ever going to satisfy it for the local-node case).

**Implementation:**
- `SerialCaptureSource.set_region(region: str) -> dict` (`src/capture/serial_source.py`) -- validates the region NAME against the real enum (`config_pb2.Config.LoRaConfig.RegionCode.Value(region)`, ValueError on typo rather than silently writing 0/UNSET), sets it, calls `writeConfig("lora")`, updates `self._radio_info["region"]` immediately (same immediate-cache-update reasoning as `set_owner()`, since the device's own NodeInfo round-trip isn't guaranteed to reflect it right away).
- `PUT /api/config/serial/region` (`src/api/routes/serial_config_routes.py`) -- resolves the source by label, 503 if not connected, 400 if the device rejects it, 200 with `{"saved": true, "region": ...}` on success. Deliberately NOT persisted to `local.yaml` (unlike the name fields, which use `_persist_serial_identity` so a later-swapped-in blank stick gets renamed automatically on reconnect) -- region durably lives in the device's own NVS, and re-applying it to a swap-in is a much rarer need than a rename; kept simple rather than over-building.
- Frontend: new "LoRa region" `<select>` (all 37 region codes except `UNSET`, which isn't something you'd deliberately pick) + "Set Region" button per device row in `serial_card.js`, shown whenever connected (not just while UNSET, so it doubles as a way to change region later too), with an explicit warning hint specifically while `region === 'UNSET'`.

**Verification (Mac, stub-based)**: built a fake `meshtastic.protobuf.config_pb2.Config.LoRaConfig.RegionCode` (minimal `.Value()`/`.Name()`) and a fake `interface.localNode` to exercise the REAL `SerialCaptureSource.set_region()` method directly -- confirmed a valid region correctly mutates `localConfig.lora.region` and calls `writeConfig("lora")` exactly once, confirmed an unknown region name is rejected cleanly (no protobuf exception leaking out), confirmed the not-connected case short-circuits without touching `iface`. Route exercised end-to-end with fake sources for all three outcomes (success, device-rejected/400, not-connected/503). `node --check`/`ast.parse` clean; `tests/test_html_assets.py` 7/7; changelog re-parses (26 sections). **LIVE-VERIFIED on the real freshly-flashed Heltec V3, same day**: set region to EU_433 through the actual UI -- readouts immediately updated to FREQUENCY 433.875 MHz, REGION EU_433, confirming the whole live-write path (Node.writeConfig("lora") over the already-open connection, no port release needed) works end-to-end on real hardware.

**Follow-on, same conversation**: user found the Name+Region boxes looked like nested boxes-within-boxes (`.cfg-mc-identity` gives each block its own border/background; two stacked back-to-back looked cluttered) -- fixed by merging Region into the SAME box as Name, separated by a new thin `.cfg-mc-identity__divider` rule, rather than two separate boxes. `_regionEditHtml` renamed to `_regionEditFragment` (no wrapper div of its own now, spliced into `_identityHtml`'s existing box).

User then asked the bigger question: "what else needs setting" for a fresh Meshtastic node (modem preset, hop limit, Bluetooth PIN). Answered from real source (not guessed): modem preset already defaults to `LONG_FAST` (matches their other node), hop limit defaults to 3 (fine), channel/PSK is already the public default (fine for general monitoring). Bluetooth was the one genuine open question -- confirmed via `meshtastic/protobufs`' real `BluetoothConfig` message: `enabled` (bool) + `mode` (`RANDOM_PIN`=0 default / `FIXED_PIN`=1 / `NO_PIN`=2) + `fixed_pin` (uint32). Rather than Claude picking one on the user's behalf, user explicitly asked for a UI control so **the user decides** -- built exactly that.

**Bluetooth control added** (same live-connection pattern as region, same session):
- `SerialCaptureSource.set_bluetooth(enabled, mode=None, fixed_pin=None)` (`src/capture/serial_source.py`) -- same `Node.writeConfig("bluetooth")` mechanism, same confirmed-non-blocking guarantee as region/set_owner. Validates PIN range (0-999999, a 6-digit PIN) and mode name against the real enum before writing.
- `_read_radio_info()` extended to also read back `bluetooth.enabled`/`bluetooth.mode` (new `_config_pb2` import scoped to its own try block, deliberately not reusing the lora block's import binding, for defensive independence -- best-effort read, matching the file's existing philosophy).
- `PUT /api/config/serial/bluetooth` (`src/api/routes/serial_config_routes.py`) -- same shape as the region route (503 not-connected, 400 device-rejected, 200 success). Not persisted to `local.yaml`, same reasoning as region.
- Frontend: checkbox (Bluetooth enabled) + pairing-mode `<select>` (hidden when disabled) + fixed-PIN number input (hidden unless mode is FIXED_PIN) + Set Bluetooth button, spliced into the SAME shared identity/region box (third fragment, `_bluetoothEditFragment`, another `.cfg-mc-identity__divider` seam). Show/hide wiring is plain JS toggling `hidden` on the wrapper `<label>`s -- already covered by the earlier `.cfg-field[hidden] { display: none; }` CSS fix from the POCSAG card work, no new CSS bug here.

**Verification (Mac, stub-based)**: built a fake `meshtastic.protobuf.config_pb2.Config.BluetoothConfig.PairingMode` and fake `interface.localNode` to exercise the REAL `set_bluetooth()` method directly -- confirmed disable-only (mode left untouched), confirmed enable+FIXED_PIN+PIN value all set together in one `writeConfig` call, confirmed out-of-range PIN and unknown mode name both rejected cleanly. Route exercised end-to-end for all three outcomes. `node --check`/`ast.parse` clean; `tests/test_html_assets.py` 7/7; changelog re-parses (26 sections). **Not yet live-tested against the real Heltec V3** -- next step when picked back up.

**User asked "what else needs setting" three times, then explicitly said "i want them ... if we can send these to the serial meshtastic we want it"** -- built Modem Preset + NodeInfo/Telemetry broadcast intervals too, same session, same live-connection pattern. Also fixed a real visual bug the user caught: even after merging Name+Region+Bluetooth into one `.cfg-mc-identity` box, they still reported "the blocks are still there" -- re-verified the actual file (one wrapping div, confirmed structurally correct) and advised a hard browser refresh (Cmd+Shift+R), since browsers cache CSS separately from JS and the divider rule may not have reloaded even though the JS did. Root cause not fully confirmed either way as of this note.

**Verified against real Meshtastic protobuf source before implementing** (not guessed): `node_info_broadcast_secs` confirmed to live under the `Device` config message (not `lora`), defaults to 900s (15 min); `telemetry.device_update_interval`/`environment_update_interval` confirmed to be MODULE config (`set_module_config.telemetry`, a different `writeConfig()` config_name than top-level sections). Full real `ModemPreset` enum fetched too (17 values including deprecated `LONG_SLOW`/`VERY_LONG_SLOW` and newer `LITE_*`/`NARROW_*`/`TINY_*`/`MEDIUM_TURBO` presets not shown on the concentrator's own picker) -- deliberately exposed only the SAME 10 named presets the concentrator's own Radio page already shows, for consistency, skipping "Custom" (raw spread-factor/bandwidth/coding-rate, not a named preset).

**Implementation** (same pattern as region/Bluetooth, all in the same 3 files):
- `SerialCaptureSource.set_modem_preset(preset)` -- sets `use_preset=True` + `modem_preset`, `writeConfig("lora")` (same config section as region -- both live on `localConfig.lora`).
- `SerialCaptureSource.set_broadcast_intervals(node_info_secs=None, telemetry_secs=None)` -- either field optional (no-op if both omitted), validates 0-86400s range, writes `device.node_info_broadcast_secs` via `writeConfig("device")` and/or `telemetry.device_update_interval` via `writeConfig("telemetry")` -- confirmed via a fake node these fire as TWO separate `writeConfig()` calls when both fields given, matching the real dispatch table's per-section-name behavior.
- `_read_radio_info()` extended a third time to read back `node_info_broadcast_secs`/`telemetry_device_update_interval` (own try/except blocks, best-effort, matching the file's established philosophy).
- Two new routes: `PUT /api/config/serial/modem-preset`, `PUT /api/config/serial/broadcast-intervals` (`src/api/routes/serial_config_routes.py`) -- same 503/400/200 shape as region/Bluetooth.
- Frontend: two more fragments (`_modemPresetEditFragment`, `_broadcastIntervalsEditFragment`) spliced into the SAME shared identity box as Name/Region/Bluetooth, each with its own `.cfg-mc-identity__divider` seam. Broadcast intervals UI works in MINUTES (matching the concentrator cards' own convention) and converts to/from seconds for the actual API calls.

**Verification (Mac, stub-based)**: built fake `ModemPreset`/`localConfig.device`/`moduleConfig.telemetry` objects to exercise both REAL methods directly -- confirmed preset validation + `use_preset`/`modem_preset` both set correctly in one `writeConfig("lora")` call; confirmed broadcast intervals fire the correct SEPARATE `writeConfig()` calls per section, confirmed a partial update (only one field given) only touches that one section and leaves the other's `writeConfig` uncalled, confirmed out-of-range values rejected. Both routes exercised end-to-end for success + rejection cases. `node --check`/`ast.parse` clean; `tests/test_html_assets.py` 7/7; changelog re-parses (26 sections). **None of these three are strictly required** -- region was the only actual TX blocker; these were built because the user explicitly wanted full control over everything technically possible on this stick, not because Meshpoint's own dashboard functionality depends on them.

**Full restyle, same day, after the user pushed back three times** ("this looks so strange", "how many minutes is 35791", "look at the other cards configuration radio it should look like that we want it uniform"). Root-caused by actually reading `radio_card.js`/`nodeinfo_config_card.js` (Configuration -> Radio's own cards) rather than continuing to guess at CSS fixes: those cards render every field as a PLAIN `.cfg-field` directly inside one `.cfg-card`, with NO intermediate bordered sub-box -- and Modem Preset there is a `.cfg-chip-row` of pill buttons (a real, already-existing, reusable CSS component: `.cfg-chip`/`.cfg-chip--selected`/`.cfg-chip--off`), not a dropdown. My earlier "merge into one box with dividers" fix was still fundamentally the wrong shape -- it fixed the box-COUNT but not the fact that Meshpoint has no "boxed sub-group" convention anywhere else at all.

**Full rewrite**: removed `_regionEditFragment`/`_modemPresetEditFragment`/`_broadcastIntervalsEditFragment`/`_bluetoothEditFragment` (all four, along with the `.cfg-mc-identity__divider` CSS rule) and replaced with one `_radioControlsHtml(live)` returning plain `.cfg-field`s as a sibling to `_identityHtml`/`_readoutsHtml` in the device row template (not nested inside `_identityHtml`'s box at all anymore -- `_identityHtml` reverted to its original pre-existing form, untouched). Modem preset and BOTH broadcast intervals (NodeInfo, Telemetry) now use `.cfg-chip-row` + a "Custom (minutes)" fallback input, verbatim copying `NodeInfoConfigCard`'s own `_renderChips`/`_setActiveChip` interaction pattern (click a chip -> fills + highlights; typing a number highlights a matching chip or clears selection) via two new methods, `_wireRadioControls`/`_wireIntervalChips`. Region stays a plain `<select>` (37 options too many for chips; matches that Radio's own region field is *also* a plain select, not chips). Bluetooth's checkbox/mode-select/PIN-input show-hide wiring carried over unchanged (already flat, just no longer boxed).

Backend entirely untouched by this pass -- same 3 routes, same `SerialCaptureSource` methods, same wire format; this was purely a frontend HTML/CSS restructure. Caught and fixed one duplicate-docstring artifact from a line-range-based file rewrite before finalizing (`grep -c` sanity check on the static declarations after editing, matching this codebase's general discipline about verifying a large mechanical edit actually applied cleanly rather than assuming it did).

**The "35791 minutes" issue** was not specifically root-caused (no live device access) but is structurally addressed either way: it now displays in the SAME "Custom (minutes)" fallback slot `NodeInfoConfigCard` already uses for exactly this situation (a value that doesn't match a fixed chip), rather than being the ONLY way to enter a value. Worth a live check next time the actual device is available, to see whether that number is a real device-reported value or a units bug on the read side.

**Verification**: `node --check` clean; `grep` confirmed zero leftover references to the four removed methods/the removed CSS class; `tests/test_html_assets.py` 7/7; changelog re-parses (26 sections); backend `ast.parse` clean (confirming truly untouched). **Not yet live-viewed** -- next Pi visit should confirm this actually reads as "uniform with the rest of the app" the way the user asked for, and that the chip-row click/custom-input interaction works smoothly for real.

**LIVE-VERIFIED, same conversation**: user's next screenshot confirmed the restyle actually worked -- Region/Modem Preset (chip row, LongFast highlighted)/NodeInfo interval (chip row, 3h highlighted)/Telemetry interval all rendered flat, matching the Radio page. Exactly ONE box remained: the pre-existing Name section. Root cause found immediately this time (learned from the earlier back-and-forth): `.cfg-field--inline` (CSS) carries its OWN `border`/`padding`/`border-radius` -- originally added for the Radio page's frequency-mode radio-button fieldset, where a border around a small inline group makes sense, but ALSO used on "Long name"/"Short name" (Serial) and "Set callsign"/"Set web password"/"WiFi SSID"/"WiFi password" (POCSAG, from earlier in this session) where it just wraps ONE label+input pair -- giving each of those its own second, nested box inside the already-boxed `.cfg-mc-identity` container.

**Fixed by removing `.cfg-field--inline` (keeping `.cfg-field`) from all 6 affected labels** -- 2 in `serial_card.js` (Long name, Short name) + 2 more caught proactively in the same file (Bluetooth Pairing mode/Fixed PIN, which had the identical class combo and would have shown the same bug) + 4 in `pocsag_serial_card.js` (Callsign, Web password, WiFi SSID, WiFi password -- checked proactively since it uses the exact same `.cfg-mc-identity` pattern from earlier this session, without waiting for the user to find it independently there too). All now render as plain stacked label-then-input fields, no border, matching Baud Rate's existing (never-boxed) styling on the same page.

**General lesson reinforced**: when a "modifier" CSS class is reused for a visually different purpose (here: `--inline` meant "put a border around this whole inline group" in one place, but "just lay label+input out in a row" was assumed elsewhere), grep for every OTHER place that class is used before considering a fix complete -- this is the second time in one styling pass that a class turned out to be shared more broadly than the one spot being fixed.

**Correct final reading**: the user never wanted "no boxes anywhere" -- they wanted CONSISTENT, INTENTIONAL boxes: whatever grouping convention the rest of the app already uses (a proper `.cfg-card` with a title + hint, exactly like Configuration -> Radio's own card), reused for logical sub-groups WITHIN one device row, not a different-looking ad-hoc box (`.cfg-mc-identity`) invented just for this. The earlier "make it flat" instruction was really "stop using a box style that exists nowhere else" -- once shown the option of using the REAL shared `.cfg-card` pattern instead, boxing came back, just done right this time.

**Lesson for next time a similar "make it look like X" request comes in**: when the user references a SPECIFIC existing page/URL as "look exactly like this", go read that page's actual source (classes, structure) before guessing at a fix -- both real fixes in this whole arc (`.cfg-field--inline` root cause, and this final `.cfg-card` structure) only landed once the concentrator's own Radio/NodeInfo card source was actually read, not assumed from a screenshot description.

**"MeshCore firmware" flash card added to Configuration → MeshCore, 2026-07-30 (same day, right after finishing the Serial page's styling arc).** User: "lets start again with a flash card on the bottom so we can flash companions", pointing at `github.com/meshcore-dev/MeshCore`. Same overall feature as the Meshtastic firmware card (no compiling, download official release, flash with esptool, curated board list, confirm-modal-gated, NDJSON output) -- but two real MeshCore-specific things had to be figured out first, both verified against the real live repo/release rather than assumed:

- **User initially suggested `meshcore-cli flash --device <port> --firmware <type>`** -- checked by actually installing `meshcore-cli` (pip) into a scratch dir and reading its real `-h` output: **no `flash` subcommand exists** in the current released version (v1.5.7). Reported back and proceeded with the same esptool-direct approach as Meshtastic, per user's own follow-up ("i think we need togo the esptool way").
- **MeshCore's release layout is actually SIMPLER than Meshtastic's**: downloaded a real `Heltec_v3_companion_radio_usb-*-merged.bin` and inspected its raw bytes -- starts with the ESP32 image magic byte (`0xE9`) at offset 0, confirming the whole file is meant for a single `write-flash ... 0x0 <file>`, no second littlefs file or per-board offset metadata (`.mt.json` equivalent) needed at all. Confirmed by fetching `merge-bin.py` from the real repo (uses `esptool merge_bin` with `$ESP32_APP_OFFSET` as the last image, standard single-file-image convention).
- **Real gotcha found and designed around**: MeshCore tags THREE separate GitHub releases per version bump (`companion-vX.Y.Z`, `repeater-vX.Y.Z`, `room-server-vX.Y.Z`), confirmed by listing `/releases` directly -- each has its own distinct asset list. `/releases/latest` returns whichever published most recently, which happens to be `companion-` each cycle right now but isn't guaranteed. New code fetches the releases LIST and explicitly filters for the newest `companion-`-tagged one. **Flagged but did not fix**: this project's own pre-existing "Check for updates" feature on the same Configuration → MeshCore page (`meshcore_config_routes.py`, from a much earlier session) DOES trust `/releases/latest` directly -- a latent bug, out of scope for this feature, left for the user to decide whether to fix later.

**Implementation** (`src/api/routes/meshcore_firmware_routes.py`, new file, mirrors `meshtastic_firmware_routes.py`'s shape almost exactly): curated board list reuses the SAME slugs as the Meshtastic card (`heltec-v3`, `tlora-v2-1-1_6`) mapped to MeshCore's own asset-filename prefixes (`Heltec_v3`, `LilyGo_TLora_V2_1_1_6`) and esptool chip names -- confirmed both boards have real matching MeshCore companion-USB assets in the live release. Cache lives under `data/meshcore-firmware/<board>/<release-tag>/` (same `/opt/meshpoint/data/` convention as the Meshtastic firmware cache, learned from the earlier `/opt/meshtastic-firmware` permission bug -- got this right from the start this time, no repeat mistake). Flash command: `esptool --chip <chip> --port <port> --baud 921600 write-flash --erase-all 0x0 <merged.bin>` -- single file, single address, simpler than Meshtastic's two-file command. Same release-before/reconnect-after handling around a connected `MeshcoreUsbCaptureSource` (confirmed it has the identical `name`/`connected`/`stop()`/`start()` shape as `SerialCaptureSource`/`DapnetSerialSource` before relying on it). Frontend: new "MeshCore firmware" card added to `meshcore_card.js` (now 3 cards total: USB capture sources, MeshCore Companion, MeshCore firmware), device picker only shown with 2+ configured companions, `render()`'s device-picker call placed BEFORE the `if (!mc.connected) return` early-return path so it still populates even when the primary companion happens to be disconnected.

User's own answered concern mid-build: "but what if its empty the device or it has meshtastic" -- confirmed `--erase-all` (full chip wipe, not just app partition) handles both a blank board and one currently running a completely different firmware identically, same reasoning already proven live on the Meshtastic card's own repurposing of the DAPNET Heltec V3.

**Verification (Mac, real network calls)**: `ast.parse`/`node --check` clean; `_ensure_board_firmware_cached_sync` exercised for REAL against the live `meshcore-dev/MeshCore` releases list for both curated boards (correct tag/chip, cache-hit path near-instant on second call); full flash route exercised end-to-end with a stand-in `esptool` command and a fake connected `MeshcoreUsbCaptureSource`, confirming stop/start behavior, correct single-file/single-address esptool argument construction, and 400 rejection for both an unknown board and an unconfigured device label; `tests/test_html_assets.py` 7/7; changelog re-parses (26 sections). **Not yet flashed onto real hardware** -- next step when picked back up.

## CHANGELOG.md technical detail archive — v0.7.9 section (archived 2026-07-31, full detail moved out of the public changelog into this file per user request)

docs/CHANGELOG.md was rewritten to be short and user-facing; this section preserves the original detailed technical narrative (root causes, file paths, verification steps, decision history) for future debugging/session-continuity reference, since that's genuinely useful and shouldn't just be deleted. Verbatim copy of the pre-rewrite `### v0.7.9 (July 2026)` section follows.

### v0.7.9 (July 2026)

First tagged release of the javastraat/meshpoint fork: LoRaWAN sniffing, multi-radio capture, the RTL-SDR web listener, and a dashboard self-update repair -- plus everything from upstream's own v0.7.7 (backup/restore, RF Environment tab, mesh broadcast cadence, operator tools; merged, bullets below). Numbered 0.7.9 rather than 0.7.7: upstream is about to tag their own v0.7.8 (absorbing some of this fork's contributions) and likely a v0.7.9 after that, so this fork's version tracks its own progress past upstream's last merged release instead of colliding with upstream's own in-flight numbering. Run `install.sh` when upgrading: new sudoers rules for backup restore. **Upgrade note:** boxes on v0.7.6 cannot fetch this release from the dashboard (that is the bug being fixed); one manual round on the gateway is required: `cd /opt/meshpoint && sudo git fetch origin main && sudo git reset --hard origin/main && sudo systemctl restart meshpoint`. The restart installs the corrected sudoers rules; Check/Apply works from the dashboard again afterwards.

#### LoRaWAN sniffing (SX1302)

- **Passive LoRaWAN capture on EU868.** Five real 125 kHz LoRaWAN channels (867.9–868.7 MHz, sync word 0x34) on SX1302 ch0–ch4 while Meshtastic stays on the 250 kHz service channel (869.525 MHz, 0x2B) — dual sync word via direct service-channel register writes after `lgw_start()`.
- **LoRaWAN MAC decoder.** Join-Request, Data Up, and Rejoin frames parsed (DevEUI/AppEUI, DevAddr, FCnt, FPort, MIC); payloads stay encrypted (no session keys), listen-only.
- **LoRaWAN dashboard page.** Devices, recent packets, and stats views backed by `GET /api/lorawan/devices`, `/api/lorawan/packets`, `/api/lorawan/stats`.
- **Strict isolation.** LoRaWAN traffic is never relayed and never enters the mesh node roster or telemetry store; router checks LoRaWAN before Meshtastic to avoid false positives.
- **CSV export on every protocol page.** An Export button on the LoRaWAN, Meshtastic, and MeshCore pages downloads the active tab's dataset — all captured packets, or the full device/node/contact census (not just the last 100 on screen). Streamed row-by-row from the database so a full-table packets export never buffers in memory; UTF-8 with a BOM so Excel renders the emoji-heavy MeshCore names; packet exports carry the decoded payload as a JSON cell, and LoRaWAN additionally flattens DevEUI/FCnt/FPort/MIC into their own columns for coverage and frame-counter-gap analysis. Six new `GET /api/{protocol}/export/{packets,census}.csv` endpoints (viewer-open, authenticated by the session cookie).
- **FPort/FCnt show up in the packets log.** The LoRaWAN page's FPort and FCnt columns were permanently "--": the API read the decoded payload with underscored key names (`f_cnt`) while the decoder stores them without (`fcnt`). The frame counter and port now display for every data packet.
- **LoRaWAN packet-detail decrypt state now matches the live dashboard feed.** `GET /api/lorawan/packets` now returns each row's persisted `decrypted` flag, so opening the same packet from the LoRaWAN page and from Dashboard no longer disagrees on "Decrypt: Success" vs "No matching key".
- **LoRaWAN packet detail keeps metadata visible when payload keys are missing.** For encrypted LoRaWAN uplinks without app-session keys, Packet detail now still shows the decoded MAC/header JSON (`dev_addr`, `fcnt`, `fport`, `mic`, etc.) instead of hiding it behind only "No matching key"; modem CR is also suppressed on LoRaWAN rows to keep Dashboard and LoRaWAN-tab modals visually aligned.
- **Clicking a node name inside a Messages thread now opens the same node detail drawer as the dashboard/protocol tabs.** Works for the chat header's contact name (DM threads only — a channel's header is the channel, not a node) and for each received message's sender label in both DMs and channels. DM sender IDs were already reliable (`msg.node_id` is the one contact); channel/broadcast messages needed a small backend addition first — the server already looked up a broadcast message's real sender via `packet_repo.get_source_id_by_packet_id()` just to build its display name (`message_name_resolver.py`'s `_resolve_broadcast_sender`) and then discarded the ID, so the frontend had no reliable node ID to click through to for a channel message. Now stashes it as `source_id` on the returned message dict alongside the existing `node_name`. **Fixed same day, found live**: channel sender names still weren't clickable after that first pass — `_resolve_broadcast_sender()` (the only place setting `source_id`) was only ever called when a message had no already-resolved name, but real channel messages almost always already carry one from when they were stored, so the lookup — and `source_id` — was skipped for the common case. Now always resolves the sender ID (still preferring the stored name for display when one exists).
- **LoRaWAN Devices and Meshtastic Nodes tabs now show a "(N total)" / "(N of M)" count next to their search box**, matching the count MeshCore's Contacts tab already had.
- **Search filter on the MeshCore Contacts tab.** Same `.lw-search` widget as LoRaWAN Devices and Meshtastic Nodes, matching contact ID or name; the "(N total)" count now reads "(N of M)" while a search is active. Rounds out the search rollout across all three protocol pages.
- **Search box was leaking onto the Recent Packets tab on LoRaWAN/Meshtastic.** `.lw-search-wrap` set `display: inline-flex` unconditionally, which silently beats the browser's own `[hidden] { display: none }` rule (author CSS always wins over the user-agent stylesheet, regardless of selector specificity) — so the tab-switch code was correctly toggling `hidden` on the element, but it stayed visibly on screen and unfiltering on the packets view. Added an explicit `.lw-search-wrap[hidden] { display: none; }` override.
- **MeshCore Contacts tab no longer paginates.** Removed the 50-per-page click-through (`_renderNodePage`, the Prev/Next controls) — all fetched contacts now render in one list, same as the Meshtastic Nodes and LoRaWAN Devices tabs, clearing the way for a search filter across the whole contact list next rather than one page at a time. The "(N total)" count next to the tab stays.
- **Search filter on the LoRaWAN Devices tab, now also on Meshtastic Nodes.** A search box (matching device ID/name or packet type) filters the list client-side, with a clear (×) button that appears once you've typed something; the query persists across the 15-second auto-refresh instead of resetting. Piloted on LoRaWAN first, then rolled onto the Meshtastic Nodes tab (matching node ID or name) — same `.lw-search` widget, no new CSS needed since both panels already share `lorawan.css`. MeshCore is next.
- **Service channel RF chain fix.** ch8 now picks the correct radio chain from its frequency instead of hardcoded RF0.

#### DAPNET (POCSAG companion)

- **New Networks → DAPNET page and capture source**, completing the `extra/pocsag_companion` integration started earlier (Configuration → POCSAG's USB device list). `src/capture/dapnet_source.py` (`DapnetSerialSource`) reads newline-delimited JSON pages off the companion board's serial connection in a background thread (pyserial's `readline()` is blocking) and feeds them through a new `Protocol.DAPNET` alongside the existing Meshtastic/MeshCore/LoRaWAN protocols — one source per configured device, named `dapnet_<label>` (or bare `dapnet`), same convention as Serial/MeshCore. Adding `pocsag_serial` to `capture.sources` (the existing Configuration → POCSAG checkbox) spins these up. New `GET /api/dapnet/{capcodes,packets,stats}` + CSV exports, structured like LoRaWAN's (a one-way receive protocol, no conversations) but keyed on capcode instead of DevEUI, with no RF signal columns — the companion board reports none over its JSON protocol. Page named "DAPNET" rather than "POCSAG" deliberately: the Listener tab already has an older, unrelated "POCSAG" RTL-SDR passive decoder (different code path entirely); this new page specifically talks to the real DAPNET paging network via the companion's own bidirectional serial connection.
- **DAPNET capcode filters** — DAPNET's own network housekeeping/time-sync beacons repeat every couple of minutes on a handful of fixed, well-known capcodes; two new independently-configurable tiers (`Configuration → POCSAG`'s new "DAPNET capcode filters" card, `dapnet.blacklist_capcodes` / `dapnet.ignore_capcodes` in `local.yaml`) keep that noise manageable without an extra service restart. Blacklisted capcodes still show live on the DAPNET page (over the existing dashboard WebSocket) so the decoder/network can be confirmed still alive, but are never written to the database or counted in stats/relay/MQTT; ignored capcodes are dropped completely. New `PUT /api/config/dapnet`, applied immediately (the coordinator reads the config fresh on every packet, no capture-source restart needed).
- **DAPNET sidebar link only appears once the POCSAG capture source is enabled.** A new `data-requires-source` sidebar-hiding mechanism (`sidebar/sidebar_controller.js`, `_applySourceGating()`) checks `capture.sources` from `GET /api/config` and hides gated nav items entirely — independent of the existing role-based `data-requires-section` gating, which is about permissions, not capture-source state. First use of this pattern; available for any future feature that should stay hidden until its capture source is turned on.
- **DAPNET sidebar icon replaced** — the original glyph (a rounded rect + arc handle) read as a briefcase, not a pager. Swapped for an actual pager shape (body, screen, three buttons, antenna stub).
- **Long DAPNET page text no longer gets cut off.** The Recent Pages/Capcodes tables reused LoRaWAN's `lw-table` CSS, which forces `table-layout: fixed` + single-line ellipsis truncation sized for short DevEUI/RSSI columns — DAPNET's free-text message column (FT8/PSK-reporter-style pages can run 80+ characters) was silently truncating mid-sentence. New `.lw-table--dapnet-packets`/`.lw-table--dapnet-capcodes` CSS use `table-layout: auto` with a wrapping text column instead.
- **DAPNET page wasn't scrollable.** Its `.section` was missing from the CSS rule that opts specific pages out of the shared parent's `overflow: hidden` (LoRaWAN/Meshtastic/MeshCore were already listed there).
- **`meshpoint logs` no longer shows a fake "perfect signal" bar for DAPNET packets.** `print_packet()` defaulted a missing `signal` to `rssi=0.0` for display, and 0.0 dBm clamps to the *best* end of the RSSI bar's scale — every DAPNET line (which genuinely has no RSSI/SNR at all) rendered a full green bar as if reception were excellent. Now shows `--` for both fields and an empty bar when there's no real signal object, and the decoded page text is now included in the line's summary (previously blank — no `_payload_summary()` case existed for the `dapnet_*` packet types), matching every other protocol's log line.
- **Companion firmware + topbar chip: DAPNET status at a glance.** `extra/pocsag_companion.ino` gained a `{"cmd":"status"}` serial command (reply: `{"type":"status","board":...,"callsign":...,"freq":...}`), compile-verified on both TTGO and Heltec targets and OTA-reflashed. `DapnetSerialSource` sends this once at connect (not a periodic broadcast — keeps the shared serial line free of chatter that could be mistaken for a decoded page) and caches the reply. New topbar chip (`TopbarDapnetChip`, reuses the existing `.topbar-serial` CSS wholesale — same visual language as the Meshtastic USB chip, just callsign instead of node ID and board name instead of modem preset) shows one badge per configured companion, fed by a new `dapnet_status` array in `GET /api/config` (distinct from the pre-existing `dapnet` key, which is the saved blacklist/ignore config — a same-named key would have silently collided). Hidden entirely when no POCSAG companion is configured, same as the sidebar link.
- **Configuration → POCSAG now shows the same live companion readouts as Serial/MeshCore** — Callsign, Frequency, and Hardware tiles per device, reusing the shared `cfg-mc-readout` tile styling and sourced from the same `dapnet_status` array the topbar chip already reads. Smaller tile set than MeshCore's on purpose: POCSAG is fixed-frequency FSK, not LoRa, so there's no bandwidth/SF/TX-power equivalent, and the companion's status reply carries no firmware version.
- **Fixed: capcodes newly added to either DAPNET filter tier kept showing in Recent Pages history.** Both `blacklist_capcodes` and `ignore_capcodes` promise "never stored", but the coordinator's per-packet check only ever stopped *future* pages from being written — a page already sitting in the `packets` table from before a capcode was added to either list just kept showing up forever, since Recent Pages reads straight from storage. `PUT /api/config/dapnet` now also purges (`PacketRepository.delete_dapnet_capcodes`) any already-stored rows for the union of both saved lists, so the promise holds immediately instead of only going forward.
- **Operator callsign is now settable from Configuration → POCSAG, not only the companion's own WiFi page.** `extra/pocsag_companion.ino` gained a `{"cmd":"set_callsign"}` serial command (same validation cascade and NVS persistence as its existing `/api/callsign` web endpoint), and `DapnetSerialSource` gained real request/response plumbing (`send_command()` — one command in flight at a time, matched by reply `"type"`, 5s timeout) to support it, since the wire protocol was fire-and-forget-only until now (the one-shot status query never needed to await a specific reply). New `PUT /api/config/dapnet/callsign` (`src/api/routes/dapnet_config_routes.py`) resolves the companion by label and relays the command; a successful reply updates the cached status immediately so the readout tile and topbar chip reflect it without waiting for another status query. Nothing persists on the Meshpoint side — the callsign lives entirely in the companion's own NVS, same as a save made directly on its own dashboard. **Live-verified**: callsign changed to a test value and back from the dashboard, confirmed matching on the companion's own web interface both times.
- **Configuration → POCSAG's readout tiles gained a "Web UI" link to the companion's own dashboard.** `sendStatusReply()`'s one-shot reply now also includes `hostname`/`wifi_ip` — deliberately only static-ish fields (unchanged for the life of the WiFi connection), unlike a counter or uptime value, which would freeze at whatever it was at connect time and never update again since this query only ever fires once. TX count/uptime/heap were considered and explicitly deferred pending a periodic-poll design (this query is one-shot by design, to keep the shared serial line free of chatter that could be mistaken for a decoded page). The link prefers the IP as its actual target (mDNS resolution isn't always reliable client-side) but labels it with the hostname, which is what stays stable across a DHCP lease renewal. Topbar chip intentionally left compact — hostname/IP only show on the config page.
- **DAPNET status now polls periodically, surfacing TX count/last-TX-result/uptime.** The `{"cmd":"status"}` query (previously one-shot, at connect only) now repeats every `dapnet.status_poll_interval_s` (default 60s, user-editable from Configuration → POCSAG's "DAPNET settings" card — changing it needs a service restart, unlike the two capcode lists in the same card) — still request/response, the companion never pushes this unsolicited. `extra/pocsag_companion.ino`'s reply gained `tx_count`/`last_tx_ok`/`uptime_ms`, all genuinely live now that the query repeats; the companion's own `txCount`/`lastTxOk` globals needed the same `extern` forward-declaration treatment as `prefs` did for the callsign command, since they're likewise declared later in the file than `sendStatusReply()`. Two new readout tiles on Configuration → POCSAG: TX Count and Last TX (Never/OK/Failed). **A real concurrency bug was caught and fixed while building this**: `DapnetSerialSource.send_command()` had no locking, since until now only one command was ever realistically in flight (the one-shot status query, or an occasional manual callsign save). Adding a 60s recurring timer meant it would eventually race with a manual "Set Callsign" click — the second caller would silently overwrite the first's single-slot pending-reply state, stranding it until its own timeout even though the companion answers both correctly, in order. Fixed with an `asyncio.Lock` around `send_command()`, serializing concurrent callers instead of letting them stomp each other; verified by firing 5 concurrent commands at once and confirming all 5 resolve correctly.
- **POCSAG companion's web dashboard password is now settable from Configuration → POCSAG**, same pattern as the callsign. `WEB_PASSWORD` (previously a compile-time-only `secrets.h` constant `checkAuth()` compared directly) is now a runtime value backed by NVS (falls back to the `secrets.h` default until first overridden, survives reboot once set), with a new `{"cmd":"set_web_password"}` serial command and matching `PUT /api/config/dapnet/web-password`. Handled more carefully than the callsign end to end since it's a real secret, not public ham-radio info: the companion's reply never echoes the password back (unlike callsign's confirmation, which does), Meshpoint never caches or persists it anywhere (pure relay — no `local.yaml` entry, no status-cache field, no audit-log params), and `checkSerialInput()`'s own verbatim command-echo log (which already prints every other incoming serial command in full) specifically redacts `set_web_password` lines instead. The companion's existing "Clear Settings" button now also resets the password back to the `secrets.h` default alongside callsign/screen-timeout, matching how it already handled those two.
- **New "Reset Callsign & Password" button on Configuration → POCSAG** — triggers a new `{"cmd":"reset_credentials"}` serial command (`POST /api/config/dapnet/reset-credentials`), a Meshpoint-triggerable equivalent to a slice of the companion's own "Clear Settings" button, deliberately scoped narrower: only callsign and web password reset (back to empty and the `secrets.h` default respectively), screen timeout is left untouched. Uses `prefs.remove()` per-key rather than `prefs.clear()`'s whole-namespace wipe, for exactly that reason. Guarded by the dashboard's existing themed confirm modal (`window.confirmModal`, the same one Settings → System/backup-restore/channel-delete already use — destructive, TX is blocked again until a new callsign is set); a successful reset clears the cached callsign immediately so the readout tile doesn't keep showing the old value until the next status poll.
- **WiFi SSID/password now settable from Configuration → POCSAG too, plus a serial-triggered reboot.** New `{"cmd":"set_wifi"}` (`PUT /api/config/dapnet/wifi`) and `{"cmd":"reboot"}` (`POST /api/config/dapnet/reboot`) — the missing piece for configuring a brand-new companion entirely through Meshpoint, without ever touching `secrets.h` before the first flash or opening the companion's own web dashboard: USB serial works independently of WiFi state, so a board with blank/wrong WiFi credentials is still fully reachable for this. Deliberately its own separate action, not folded into the reset/callsign/password controls — unlike those, changing WiFi takes the companion off its current network until it reboots with the new credentials, a materially bigger consequence. `WIFI_SSID`/`WIFI_PASSWORD` (previously `secrets.h` compile-time-only) are now NVS-backed runtime values the same way callsign/web-password are, but saving alone does **not** reconnect — `setupWifiNtpOta()` only ever runs once, in `setup()` — so the dashboard's save flow chains a confirm-modal-gated "reboot now?" prompt into the new reboot command afterward. The password field follows the same secret-handling rules as the web password (never cached/logged/echoed by Meshpoint; the companion's own reply only echoes the SSID back; `checkSerialInput()`'s verbatim command-echo log now redacts both `set_web_password` and `set_wifi` lines). **Known open question, not yet live-tested**: whether Meshpoint's own serial connection survives the companion's reboot depends on whether its USB-UART bridge chip stays enumerated through an ESP32 reset (likely, on both current boards) or the board re-enumerates over native USB (would need a Meshpoint service restart to reconnect, since `DapnetSerialSource` has no reconnect loop) — the reboot route's own docstring flags this explicitly.
- **Companion's own web dashboard gained Hardware and Connection cards, plus a pre-login identity line** — closes the loop on the WiFi-set feature above by making it actually verifiable without leaving the companion's own UI. Hardware: chip model/revision/cores/CPU frequency, flash size, free heap, sketch space used/free, SDK version (all built into the ESP32 core, no new dependency). Connection: SSID, IP, gateway, subnet, DNS, MAC, RSSI, hostname — everything needed to confirm a serial-set WiFi credential actually resolved correctly. Both fed by new fields on the existing `/api/status` endpoint (already polled every few seconds), not a new request. Login screen (before any password is entered) now shows callsign + hostname via a new **unauthenticated** `GET /api/whoami` — lets multiple companions on the same network be told apart at a glance; neither field is sensitive (a callsign is public ham-radio info, and the hostname is already broadcast in the clear via mDNS regardless). Also fixed two stale UI strings while in the area: the "Clear Settings" confirm/reboot modals still said "callsign and screen timeout" only, not mentioning the web password reset added earlier this session. Entirely self-contained in `extra/pocsag_companion.ino` — no Meshpoint-side code changes. Compile-verified on both boards only; TTGO flash is now at **~95.7%** (1,253,940/1,310,720 bytes, ~56.8KB headroom) — tightening with each addition this session and getting close to the point where further TTGO-side growth on this file may need to trim something first. Hardware/Connection cards moved to the front of the grid on request (pure reorder, no logic change, confirmed byte-identical compiled size on both boards).
- **Configuration → POCSAG's readout tiles now also show the companion's current WiFi SSID.** `sendStatusReply()`'s periodic reply gained `wifi_ssid` (`WiFi.SSID()`), threaded through `DapnetSerialSource`'s status cache and `GET /api/config`'s `dapnet_status` array the same way `wifi_ip`/`hostname` already were — lets you confirm a serial-set WiFi credential is actually the network it's connected to, right on the Meshpoint dashboard, not just on the companion's own web UI.
- **Fixed: the Web UI readout tile's link turned an unreadable purple once clicked.** A nested `<a>` inside a `.cfg-mc-readout__value` span has its own browser default/visited link colors, overriding the amber every other readout uses — added an explicit `color: inherit` override (same fix already applied to `.cfg-mc-readout__update-status a` elsewhere in this file).
- **Fixed: the Dashboard packet feed showed mangled From/To for DAPNET pages** (e.g. capcode `2041152` rendered as `!1152`, `broadcast` as `!cast`) **and had From/To backwards.** DAPNET has no real "sender ID" — a page is broadcast over RF and addressed *to* a capcode, not *from* one — but `dapnet_event_adapter.py` encoded it the other way round (`source_id=capcode`, `destination_id="broadcast"`), and the shared `simple_packet_feed.js`/`_fmtId()` formatter then applied Meshtastic's hex-ID shortening on top regardless of protocol. Swapped the adapter to `source_id="broadcast"`/`destination_id=capcode` (matching the real direction), updated `dapnet_routes.py`'s capcode-roster queries and `PacketRepository.delete_dapnet_capcodes`'s purge filter to key on `destination_id` instead of `source_id`, and gave `_fmtId()` a `dapnet` branch that shows both fields verbatim as plain text — no hex truncation, no "broadcast" collapsed to "!cast". **Existing DAPNET rows stored under the old (backwards) semantics are not migrated** — run the existing `scripts/clear_dapnet_packets.py --apply` once after upgrading to clear them; new pages captured after the upgrade use the corrected direction automatically.
- **Companion firmware can now be built and flashed straight from the dashboard.** `scripts/install.sh` gained a new idempotent section installing a self-contained `arduino-cli` + ESP32 toolchain under `/opt/arduino-cli` (own config, board/library data, owned by the `meshpoint` service user rather than any user's home dir, since the service account has none) — general-purpose, not POCSAG-specific, since `arduino-cli`'s bundled `esptool` can also write prebuilt Meshtastic/MeshCore `.bin` releases later. `Configuration → POCSAG` gained a "Companion firmware" card between the device list and capcode filters: a board pulldown auto-populated from whichever `BOARD_*` defines the sketch actually has (`GET /api/pocsag/firmware/targets`), and Compile/Flash buttons backed by new `POST /api/pocsag/firmware/{compile,flash}/stream` endpoints that stream `arduino-cli`'s live output as NDJSON into a collapsible panel (same wire pattern Settings → Updates' apply/stream already uses). Board target is a source-level `#define` in the sketch, not a build flag, so Compile rewrites the sketch's own `BOARD_*` toggle lines to match the chosen board first (same edit made by hand while compile-verifying both boards earlier). Flash resolves the target port server-side from the configured companion (never trusted from the browser), and — new — releases that device's live serial connection before writing and reconnects it afterward, so a flash no longer leaves DAPNET capture silently dead until a manual service restart (the exact gap hit and confirmed live while building this). A real permission bug was caught along the way: `arduino-cli`'s build cache has no `--config-file` key of its own and always resolves via `$XDG_CACHE_HOME`/`$HOME/.cache`, but `meshpoint` has no real `$HOME` (`--no-create-home`) — fixed with `Environment=XDG_CACHE_HOME=/opt/arduino-cli/cache` on the systemd unit. **Live-verified end-to-end** as the actual `meshpoint` user: compiled and flashed a real Heltec V3 companion from the CLI (proving the exact toolchain/permission model the new buttons now automate), including hitting and resolving a `/dev/ttyUSB*` renumbering gotcha after a reflash. **Two bugs found live-testing the actual card and fixed same day**: Compile's `arduino-cli` invocation was missing `-v`, so the whole ~10s+ build ran silently and only the final size summary ever appeared — the output panel looked frozen the entire time even though it was working; and the "Companion to flash" picker showed up even with only one companion configured (should auto-select and stay hidden) — `.cfg-field`'s own `display: flex` was silently beating the browser's `[hidden] { display: none }` rule, the same class of bug as the earlier LoRaWAN search-box fix; added an explicit `.cfg-field[hidden] { display: none; }` override. Also: the Board pulldown now auto-selects to match whatever board the relevant companion actually reports over its live status reply (same `board` field its Hardware readout tile already shows), instead of always defaulting to the first option — re-evaluated whenever the "Companion to flash" selection changes, and never overrides a board the user picked manually themselves. A bit more breathing room was also added between the Board field and the action buttons (scoped to this card only, not a global `.cfg-card__actions` change, which touches ~30 other action rows across the app).
- **`scripts/install.sh` now also installs a bare `esptool` command.** Not the copy already bundled inside arduino-cli's own ESP32 core (buried under `/opt/arduino-cli/data/packages/esp32/tools/esptool_py/`, never on `PATH`) — Meshtastic's own official flashing scripts (`device-install.sh`/`device-update.sh`, used to flash a spare board with official Meshtastic firmware for use as a Serial companion) expect a plain `esptool` on `PATH`, same as arduino-cli itself needed its own separate install rather than reusing another tool's private copy.
- **Configuration → Serial gained a "Meshtastic firmware" card** for repurposing a spare ESP32 board (e.g. one previously running `extra/pocsag_companion` for DAPNET) into a Meshtastic USB stick, straight from the dashboard — no compiling, since official Meshtastic firmware is PlatformIO-built upstream, not an Arduino sketch. New `GET /api/config/serial/firmware/targets` (a curated pulldown — Heltec V3, TTGO LoRa32 V2.1-1.6, TTGO T3 V3.0 TCXO — not Meshtastic's whole ~130-board catalog, just this project's actual hardware lineup) and `POST /api/config/serial/firmware/flash/stream` (`src/api/routes/meshtastic_firmware_routes.py`, new file). On flash: fetches the latest `meshtastic/firmware` GitHub release, resolves which per-chip-architecture ZIP the chosen board lives in from the release's own top-level manifest (`firmware-<version>.json`), downloads and caches just that board's `.factory.bin` (a combined bootloader+partition-table+app image meant for a from-scratch flash) and `littlefs-*.bin` under this install's own `data/` directory (alongside the SQLite DB — already excluded from `install.sh`'s rsync and already owned by the `meshpoint` service user, unlike a standalone `/opt` path, which would need its own explicit `mkdir`/`chown`) — repeat flashes of the same board/version skip the ~170MB re-download entirely. Every flash offset comes from the release's own per-board `.mt.json` metadata (also bundled in the zip), not hardcoded, so a future Meshtastic release can't silently drift out of sync with this file. Writes with the standalone `esptool` (see above) using `--erase-all`, since the board may currently hold a completely different firmware's partition layout — guarded by a confirm modal, since unlike the POCSAG card's Compile/Flash this is explicitly destructive and not reversible from here. Same NDJSON streaming/output-panel pattern as the POCSAG firmware card (shares its `.cfg-firmware-output`/`.cfg-firmware-board-field` CSS), and the same release-before/reconnect-after handling around a connected `SerialCaptureSource` so flashing doesn't leave Serial capture dead until a manual restart. **Verified against the real, live meshtastic/firmware release** (not just stubbed): downloaded and cached both a Heltec V3 (esp32s3, littlefs @ 0x670000) and a TTGO LoRa32 V2.1-1.6 (esp32, littlefs @ 0x300000) build, confirmed the cache-hit path skips re-downloading, and exercised the full flash route (stop/start around a fake connected source, correct `esptool --chip ... write-flash --erase-all 0x0 ...` argument construction) end-to-end with a stand-in command. **Live-verified on real hardware**: flashed a repurposed Heltec V3 through the actual dashboard card — factory + littlefs images written and hash-verified, hard reset, and Meshtastic's own boot screen confirmed showing on the board's LCD afterward.
- **Configuration → Serial can now set a Meshtastic USB stick's LoRa region directly**, over the same live serial connection the existing "Save Name" identity control already uses — most useful right after flashing a board fresh with the card above, since Meshtastic's factory default is region UNSET and a device won't transmit at all until one is set. New "LoRa region" pulldown + Set Region button per device row (shown whenever connected, with an explicit warning hint while region reads UNSET), backed by a new `SerialCaptureSource.set_region()` (`src/capture/serial_source.py`) and `PUT /api/config/serial/region` (`src/api/routes/serial_config_routes.py`) — same `Node.writeConfig()` AdminMessage mechanism `set_owner()` already uses, confirmed non-blocking the same way (reading meshtastic-python's own source: `writeConfig()` only waits for an ack when the target isn't the local node, which is never the case here). Not persisted to `local.yaml` like the name fields are — region lives durably in the device's own NVS, and re-applying it automatically to a swapped-in blank replacement is a much rarer need than a rename, so there's no apply-on-reconnect path (yet). The Name and Region controls now share a single box with a thin divider between them instead of two separately-bordered blocks stacked back-to-back, which looked like nested boxes-within-boxes.
- **Configuration → Serial can also set a Meshtastic USB stick's Bluetooth config** — enabled/disabled plus pairing mode (Random PIN / Fixed PIN / No PIN) and a custom PIN when Fixed PIN is chosen, same live-serial-connection mechanism as region (new `SerialCaptureSource.set_bluetooth()`, `PUT /api/config/serial/bluetooth`). Deliberately leaves the choice to the user rather than picking one on their behalf — a USB-only capture stick may not need Bluetooth at all, but someone wanting occasional phone-app access can set their own PIN instead of relying on the random one shown on a screen they may not have handy. `SerialCaptureSource._read_radio_info()` also now reads back the device's current `bluetooth.enabled`/`bluetooth.mode` for the UI to reflect. Not persisted to `local.yaml`, same reasoning as region.
- **Configuration → Serial can also set a Meshtastic USB stick's modem preset and its own NodeInfo/telemetry broadcast intervals**, all over the same live serial connection. Modem preset (`PUT /api/config/serial/modem-preset`, new `SerialCaptureSource.set_modem_preset()`) offers the same 10 named presets Configuration → Radio's own concentrator page shows (LongFast through ShortTurbo) — "Custom" (raw spread-factor/bandwidth/coding-rate) isn't exposed here. Broadcast intervals (`PUT /api/config/serial/broadcast-intervals`, new `SerialCaptureSource.set_broadcast_intervals()`) control how often the *stick itself* announces its own NodeInfo (`device.node_info_broadcast_secs`) and reports its own device telemetry (`telemetry.device_update_interval`, a module config — its own separate `writeConfig()` call) — entered in minutes in the UI, matching the concentrator cards' own convention, though this is **not the same subsystem**: those concentrator cards schedule Meshpoint's own directly-driven radio, while this is the attached stick's own independent firmware-internal timing. `_read_radio_info()` extended again to read back current values for both. None of these three are strictly required (region was the one actual blocker) — added because the user asked for full control over what's technically possible to set on a fresh node, not just the minimum to get it transmitting.
- **Fixed: Region/Bluetooth/Modem-Preset/broadcast-interval controls looked visually inconsistent with the rest of the app.** They'd each been wrapped in their own bordered `.cfg-mc-identity` box (or, after an interim fix, merged into one box with divider lines) — either way, nothing else in Configuration looks like that; every other page (Radio, NodeInfo/Telemetry broadcast interval) renders its fields as plain, unboxed `.cfg-field`s directly inside one card. Rewritten to match exactly: all four controls are now flat fields living directly in the device row (`.cfg-companion` already provides the one border a row needs), and Modem Preset plus both broadcast intervals now use the same `.cfg-chip-row` pill-button pattern as Configuration → Radio's own preset picker and its NodeInfo/Telemetry broadcast-interval cards (chip presets + a "Custom (minutes)" fallback input) instead of a raw dropdown/number box — clicking a chip fills and highlights the paired custom field, typing a number highlights a matching chip if one exists. Region stays a plain `<select>`, matching how Radio's own region field is *also* a plain select, not a chip row (too many options for chips). One nested box still remained after that pass, though — the pre-existing "Long name"/"Short name" fields (Configuration → Serial) and "Set callsign"/"Set web password"/"WiFi SSID"/"WiFi password" fields (Configuration → POCSAG) all used `.cfg-field--inline`, a class that carries its own `border`/`padding`/`border-radius` (meant for the Radio page's frequency-mode radio-button fieldset, not a single label+input pair) — giving each of those fields a second, redundant box nested inside their already-boxed `.cfg-mc-identity` container. Removed `.cfg-field--inline` from all of them across both cards; they're now plain stacked label-then-input fields like everywhere else.
- **Configuration → Serial's per-device Region/Preset/broadcast-interval/Bluetooth controls now sit in two proper sub-cards** ("Modem settings" and "Other settings"), built from the exact same `.cfg-card` → `.cfg-card__head` (title + hint) → `.cfg-form` structure Configuration → Radio's own card uses — not a repurposed `.cfg-mc-identity` box or flat fields with no grouping at all, but nested one level inside the device row alongside the pre-existing Name card, so one device reads as three peer cards (Name, Modem settings, Other settings) the same way the top of Configuration reads as a stack of peer cards.
- **Configuration → MeshCore gained a "MeshCore firmware" card**, same idea as Serial's Meshtastic-firmware card but for repurposing a spare board into a MeshCore USB companion — no compiling (official releases are prebuilt), full-chip erase first (works whether the board is blank or currently running something else, e.g. Meshtastic or `extra/pocsag_companion`), confirm-modal-gated, NDJSON-streamed output, curated board pulldown (Heltec V3, TTGO LoRa32 V2.1-1.6 — same slugs as the Meshtastic card, for consistent naming across both). New `GET /api/config/meshcore/firmware/targets` / `POST /api/config/meshcore/firmware/flash/stream` (`src/api/routes/meshcore_firmware_routes.py`, new file). MeshCore's own release layout turned out simpler than Meshtastic's: each board ships one self-contained `*-merged.bin` (confirmed by inspecting a real download — starts with the ESP32 image magic byte at offset 0), so flashing is a single `esptool write-flash --erase-all 0x0 <merged.bin>`, no second littlefs file or per-board offset metadata needed.
