One real gotcha found and handled: MeshCore tags three separate GitHub releases per version (`companion-`, `repeater-`, `room-server-`), each with its own distinct asset list — fetching `/releases/latest` directly (which the project's *existing* "Check for updates" feature on this same page does) can silently return the wrong one if a repeater/room-server release happens to publish more recently; this new code instead fetches the releases list and explicitly picks the newest `companion-`-tagged one. **Verified against the real, live MeshCore release** (not just stubbed): downloaded and cached both Heltec V3 (esp32s3) and TTGO LoRa32 V2.1-1.6 (esp32) merged images, confirmed the cache-hit path, and exercised the full flash route (stop/start around a fake connected source, correct `esptool` argument construction, unknown-board and unconfigured-device rejection) end-to-end with a stand-in command. Not yet flashed onto real hardware.
- **DAPNET's Recent Pages/Capcodes tables get two mobile/UX fixes**, both reported live off a phone screenshot. First: the page-text column used a wrapping `auto` table layout (added earlier so long pages weren't silently truncated) that, on a narrow viewport, had so little room left after the other fixed columns that `word-break` wrapped it one word (sometimes one character) per line -- reverted to the same fixed-layout, single-line-ellipsis column every other `.lw-table` already uses (`frontend/css/lorawan.css`), since truncating the inline preview is no longer a real loss once the second fix below exists. Second: clicking a Recent Pages row now opens the same full-detail popup Meshtastic/MeshCore rows already have (`window.PacketDetailModal`, `frontend/js/packet_detail_modal.js`) instead of doing nothing -- DAPNET's `/api/dapnet/packets` (and `dapnet_panel.js`'s own live-WS mirror of that shape) return `capcode`/`function`/`text` as flat top-level fields rather than the `destination_id` + nested `decoded_payload` object every other protocol's rows already carry, so the modal gained a small `_normalize()` step reshaping DAPNET's row into that common shape before building its RF/Mesh/Payload/Capture sections, plus `_payloadSummary` cases for the four DAPNET page types (`dapnet_alpha`/`dapnet_numeric` show the real text, `dapnet_tone`/`dapnet_activation` show a "no text" placeholder) and hid the "Decrypt" row for DAPNET (broadcast in the clear, no key/decrypt step to report, same reasoning already applied to MeshCore). Also fixed a small pre-existing rough edge while in there: a packet-detail layer with every row filtered out (DAPNET has no RF signal metrics at all, so its "RF" section would render as a bare heading with nothing under it) is now dropped entirely instead of showing an empty section -- a general `_buildLayer()` fix, not DAPNET-specific, though DAPNET is the first caller that actually hits it. Verified via a real (non-jsdom, hand-stubbed `document`) V8-context run: `_normalize()` correctly reshapes a flat DAPNET packet, `_payloadSummary()` returns the right content for all four page types including the two placeholder cases, the Decrypt row is absent, all-`n/a` RF rows correctly cause the whole layer to be dropped, and `PacketDetailModal.show()` completes without throwing on a real DAPNET packet shape. `node --check`/CSS-brace-balance/`test_html_assets` all clean. **Two same-day follow-on bugs, both found live on a real phone**: (1) the popup opened on a page that had just arrived over the live WebSocket feed (not yet caught up by the next 15s poll) showed no page text at all -- `dapnet_panel.js`'s `_onWsPacket()` flattens the incoming packet into `{capcode, function, text}` but was dropping `protocol`/`source_id` in the process, so `PacketDetailModal._normalize()`'s `packet.protocol === 'dapnet'` check never fired for that still-live-only row and the whole payload silently fell back to nothing; fixed by keeping `protocol`/`source_id` on the flattened object too, so a row clicked in that up-to-15s window normalizes exactly like a polled one. (2) the Type column's badge pill ("Numeric", and especially "Activation") was wider than the 76px column width inherited from LoRaWAN's own col-type (sized for its own shorter "Join"/"Data"/"Rejoin" words), so the badge overflowed and got clipped by the shared `.lw-table td`'s `text-overflow: ellipsis` -- at a glance this read as a stray dot sitting next to the badge rather than a real "…"; widened `.lw-table--dapnet-packets`/`.lw-table--dapnet-capcodes`'s own `col.col-type` to 100px so even "Activation" fits without clipping. **Third same-day follow-on**: the Capcodes tab's "Last text" column showed nothing at all on mobile, not even truncated -- unlike the Recent Pages table, Capcodes has six fixed-width columns (two "seen" time columns, id, type, frames) summing to 434px, which on its own already exceeds a phone viewport's width; under `table-layout: fixed`, `col.col-text`'s unset width -- meant to take "whatever's left" -- had nothing left to take and collapsed to effectively zero rather than growing the table wider. Gave `col.col-text` (both tables, for consistency) a 160px `min-width`, which forces the browser to actually reserve room for it and lets `.lw-table-wrap`'s pre-existing `overflow-x: auto` scroll the rest of the table into view instead -- the same horizontal scroll the other fixed columns were already relying on to be reachable on a narrow screen (visible in the reporting screenshot: First/Last seen and part of Capcode were already scrolled off to the left). **Fourth same-day follow-on, the `min-width` fix above didn't actually work** -- confirmed still broken live on the real phone even after a refresh. Root cause: `table-layout: fixed`'s column-sizing algorithm only ever consults a column's `width` (via `<col>` or the first row's cells) when deciding how much space to give it -- `min-width` isn't part of that algorithm at all, so a spec-strict engine is free to ignore it entirely and keep collapsing the column, which is exactly what happened. Switched `col.col-text` from `min-width: 160px` to a plain `width: 160px` -- the same property every other fixed column here already uses, guaranteed to participate in the sizing algorithm rather than hoping an engine honors it as a bonus constraint.

#### Setup wizard

- **Setup wizard lets you skip upstreaming entirely.** The `[4/8] API key` step now asks "Upstream data to meshradar.io?" before prompting for a key; answering no writes `upstream.enabled: false` (no API key required) instead of forcing activation, while still preserving any previously-saved key so re-enabling later doesn't require re-entering it.
- **Setup wizard can set the system hostname to match the device name.** Right after choosing a device name (`[5/8]`), on a fresh install (never on a re-run/upgrade — an existing box already has bookmarks, scripts, and SSH history tied to its hostname) the wizard offers to also set the Linux hostname to match, slugified to a valid form (lowercase, hyphens, 63-char cap) — so the box becomes reachable at `<name>.local` via the mDNS support `scripts/install.sh` now sets up. Runs `sudo hostnamectl set-hostname` and updates `/etc/hosts`' `127.0.1.1` entry to match (hostnamectl alone doesn't touch it, leaving a stale entry that causes "sudo: unable to resolve host" warnings otherwise); skipped automatically if the slug already matches the current hostname, and any failure (e.g. no privilege) is caught and logged without aborting the rest of setup.

#### Multi-radio capture (5 networks at once)

- **Multiple MeshCore USB companions.** `capture.meshcore_usb` accepts a list (up to 4) with per-stick labels; packets carry `meshcore_usb_<label>` as capture source. New `PUT /api/config/capture/meshcore-companions` replaces the list atomically; the Configuration page grew a dynamic companion section.
- **Multiple Meshtastic USB sticks.** `capture.serial` accepts the same list-plus-label shape as `meshcore_usb` (e.g. one stick on 433 MHz, one on 868 MHz), packets tagged `serial_<label>`; the legacy single `serial_port`/`serial_baud` fields keep working unchanged when the list is empty. Also fixes a latent duplicate-capture bug: meshtastic-python publishes every open USB interface's packets on one process-wide pypubsub topic, so running more than one stick without an identity check would have cross-attributed packets between devices. New Configuration → Serial page edits this list from the dashboard (add/remove/label, same shape as the MeshCore companion editor) instead of hand-editing `local.yaml`; new `PUT /api/config/capture/serial-devices`.
- **Serial Meshtastic capture crash and silent packet loss fixed.** The first time a `serial` USB source actually ran, it crashed the pipeline (`TypeError: object of type 'MeshPacket' has no len()`) — meshtastic-python always hands back the raw protobuf object, not bytes, so the old code never fell back to header reconstruction. Fixed, plus two bugs the crash was hiding: the reconstruction fallback read the wrong dict key (`encoded`/hex instead of the real `encrypted`/base64), and it required a `decoded` key that is absent by design on exactly the packets a passive sniffer cares about most — those the connected stick's own key couldn't decrypt (traffic on a channel it isn't configured for). Those were silently dropped instead of being handed to Meshpoint's own decoder/`channel_keys`.
- **Serial Meshtastic packets the connected stick decrypts itself now show their real type.** `encrypted`/`decoded` share one protobuf oneof on MeshPacket, so a packet the stick's own key successfully decrypted locally has no ciphertext left at all — these always showed as "Unknown" even though the decoded content (position, telemetry, nodeinfo, text) was sitting right there in the packet dict, discarded before Meshpoint ever saw it. `RawCapture` gained an optional `pre_decoded` field (portnum + inner payload bytes); `MeshtasticDecoder.decode()` dispatches it directly instead of attempting (and failing) to decrypt an empty body, so these packets now decode to their real `PacketType` just like concentrator-captured ones.
- **Band tag on node cards and the drawer.** Nodes now show a "433 MHz" / "868 MHz" chip derived from their latest packet's labelled capture source (`serial_433`, `meshcore_usb_868`, `concentrator`, …), so a 433/868 multi-stick setup is easy to tell apart at a glance.
- **Real region/frequency/SF/bandwidth/coding-rate for `serial` Meshtastic capture, plus a topbar badge per USB stick.** The `serial` source previously stamped every packet with a hardcoded `906.875 MHz` (a US915 placeholder) and SF11/BW250 regardless of the connected stick's actual region or preset. It now reads the stick's real config at connect time (meshtastic-python completes this handshake automatically before the connection call returns) — region, channel, primary channel name, modem preset (or the raw custom SF/BW/coding-rate when not using a named preset) — the same "read once at connect, mirrors MeshCore's `self_info` fix" pattern. New `src/radio/channel_frequency.py` computes the actual operating frequency using the same formula as `meshtastic/firmware`'s `RadioInterface.cpp` (verified against a local firmware checkout and cross-checked against a real device's observed frequency): region band, modem bandwidth, and — for the default/auto channel — a djb2 hash of the primary channel name (or the modem preset's display string when the channel name is blank), exactly reproducing the firmware's own frequency-slot selection instead of a fixed per-region guess. An explicit non-default channel, or one outside the region's valid slot range, reports `0.0` (this codebase's existing "unknown" sentinel) rather than a wrong number. New topbar badge — one small cyan chip per configured Meshtastic USB stick, laid out the same as the Meshtastic and MeshCore chips (brand, lamp, the stick's own node ID as the "call sign" slot, region, frequency, and its modem preset) — separate from the single "primary" MeshCore companion chip, since every serial device is capture-only (no TX binding to pick "the" one); reacts to a dashboard websocket drop the same way the other two chips do (amber "reconnecting" lamp, region/frequency/preset blanked) instead of silently keeping stale data on screen through a restart. New `scripts/backfill_serial_meshtastic_signal.py` corrects old rows still carrying the `906.875` placeholder.
- **Serial Meshtastic sticks no longer capture their own self-telemetry as spammy, confusing packets.** A connected stick's own periodic self-report (battery/uptime NodeInfo/Telemetry) passes through the same event stream as genuinely received packets — meshtastic-python doesn't distinguish them — and firmware's own convention (`rx_rssi == rx_snr == 0` meaning "generated locally, never actually received over the air") confirmed these had no real signal to show; they were landing in the packet feed and node counters as a confusing `-100 dBm` reading of the stick reporting on itself, roughly once a minute. The connect-time handshake now also reads the stick's own node number (`interface.myInfo.my_node_num`, no config needed) and drops any packet it originates before decode/storage/the feed/counters ever see it. The detected ID is exposed via the API and shown in the topbar badge's tooltip for visibility. New `scripts/purge_self_originated_node.py` removes historical packet/telemetry/message/node rows left over from before this fix (the drop only stops future capture, it doesn't retroactively clean the database). The drop now exempts `TEXT_MESSAGE_APP`: a chat message typed via a BLE/WiFi-connected app on the same physical stick is genuine content the user wants in the Messages panel, not a beacon, so it still reaches decode/storage even though the stick is its own "from" node for that packet — only routine self-reported telemetry/nodeinfo/position stays dropped.
- **Labelling a MeshCore companion no longer silently disables its TX/advert/status.** The dashboard's "MeshCore connected" lookup matched capture sources by exact name (`"meshcore_usb"`), which breaks the moment a companion gets a label (its name becomes `meshcore_usb_<label>`) — no crash, just a topbar stuck on "No companion" and no startup advert. Fixed to the same `startswith` rule already used for packet routing. Receive/capture was never affected, only transmit and the live-status chip.
- **MeshCore signal metadata.** Frequency/bandwidth/SF stamped from each companion's connect-time radio handshake (per stick, so 868 and 433 report their real channel), and hop count derived from `path_len` on contact/channel messages.
- **Simultaneous LoRaWAN + Meshtastic 868 + MeshCore 868/433 + Meshtastic 433.** Concentrator, two labelled MeshCore sticks, and a Meshtastic serial node run side by side; only Meshtastic is ever relayed.
- **DM replies now go out through the same radio that can actually reach the contact, not always "the" primary one.** On a multi-radio box (2+ MeshCore companions, or a concentrator plus a 433 MHz Meshtastic USB stick), every outbound reply previously routed through one fixed radio regardless of which one had actually heard the contact — confirmed live ("when sending thru a remote 433 companion i receive the message in chat... but when i reply... it never arrives"): a contact heard only on 433 MHz physically cannot receive a reply sent out on 868. New `NodeRepository.get_latest_capture_source()` looks up which capture source most recently heard a given contact; `TxService` uses it to pick the matching companion/stick and call its own send method instead of the primary's, falling back to the old fixed-primary behavior whenever there's no packet history yet or the matched source is disconnected. MeshCore channel broadcasts now fan out to every connected companion (channel keys are mesh-wide, so a broadcast should reach every mesh a companion is bridging) rather than going out on just one. Meshtastic serial USB sticks gained message-send capability for the first time (`SerialCaptureSource.send_text()`, previously admin-only: nodeinfo/owner); Meshtastic broadcasts still go out on the concentrator only, unaffected by this fix.
- **Chat header shows which physical connection a conversation is on.** A small pill next to the existing MC/MT protocol badge names the specific companion/stick (e.g. "433", "868", "Concentrator") a contact was last heard through — useful once a box has more than one radio per protocol and the protocol badge alone can't tell them apart. Backed by the same `get_latest_capture_source()` lookup as the reply-routing fix above; hidden for brand-new conversations with no packet history yet and for broadcast/channel threads (not tied to one specific connection). **Fixed same day, found live**: the pill didn't render at all on a real deployment even though the backend data was correct (verified against a real DB copy — `capture_source` resolved correctly for both a 433 and an 868 contact) — root cause was `.msg-chat__connection-badge` never getting any CSS at all, unlike its sibling `.msg-chat__protocol-badge`, so it had no background/padding/color and was effectively invisible next to the styled MC/MT badge. Added matching pill styling in `frontend/css/messaging.css`. **A second, more serious bug found the same day (real live report: "no freq shown... also it takes at least 15 sec before chat is loaded")**: `_enrich_conversations()` was awaiting the capture-source lookup once *per conversation*, sequentially — every part of the app shares one `aiosqlite` connection that funnels all DB access (including live packet writes from every capture source) through a single background-thread queue, so a dozen-plus conversations each queued up behind ongoing capture writes, visibly slowing the whole Messages page. New `NodeRepository.get_latest_capture_sources()` (batched, one query for every conversation's node_id via the same `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY source_id ...)` pattern already used elsewhere) replaces the N sequential awaits with one. **The Messages page was still slow after that fix**, tracked down to a pre-existing (not new this session) bottleneck: `MessageNameResolver._lookup_meshcore()` calls `get_contacts()` to resolve a MeshCore contact's display name, and that call is a live USB round trip to the physical companion (up to a 10 s timeout) — invoked once per conversation and once per message on a 50-message chat page, so a single page load could trigger dozens of real hardware round trips back to back. Added a 10-second cache so a page load reuses one fetch instead of one per item. **Channel/broadcast conversations now get the pill too** (previously DM-only): since packets aren't tagged with a channel number, this is scoped to "which capture source most recently heard this protocol" rather than the exact channel — coarser than the per-contact DM lookup, but still tells 868 and 433 apart, or shows "Concentrator" for Meshtastic. New `NodeRepository.get_latest_capture_sources_by_protocol()`. That backend addition alone wasn't reachable from the UI, though: the sidebar's channel rows are built client-side from `/api/messages/channels` (pure config — names/keys, no capture data) by `_channelToConvo()`, which merges in a few fields from the enriched conversations list but didn't copy `capture_source`, so a channel's pill could never render no matter what the API returned — fixed. The whole backend chain was also proven end-to-end by running the real route code against a production database copy: every DM and channel conversation resolved its correct source (DM on the 433 companion → `meshcore_usb_433`, MeshCore channels → `meshcore_usb_868`, Meshtastic channels → `concentrator`) — and then confirmed on the live deployment itself (the user pasted the real `/api/messages/conversations` response, every row carrying the right `capture_source`). **The pill now also shows in the conversation list rows** (next to each channel/DM's MC/MT badge in the sidebar), not just the open chat's header — the list is where a multi-radio setup actually scans for "which band is this on", and it was the spot the "no freq shown on channels and dm's" reports were about all along; the full source name appears as a hover tooltip. **Live-verified**, which immediately surfaced one layout follow-up: a long node name (e.g. "PD2EMC Companion 🏠") pushed the badges out of the row entirely — the name row is a flex container, so its `text-overflow: ellipsis` never actually applied to the text and long names just crushed the badge elements instead. The name now truncates with "…" in its own span while the MC/MT and connection badges always stay visible.
- **Messages page headers were permanently invisible — the panel was exactly one topbar too tall.** The chat header (contact name, protocol badge, connection pill) and the sidebar's own "Messages / + New" header had never been visible on a real deployment ("there is nothing above 2day my friend"): `.messaging` sized itself `calc(100vh - 32px)` inside a `100vh` overflow-hidden container that also holds the ~48px topbar, and opening any conversation focuses the compose input — which auto-scrolls the clipped container to reveal it, shoving both headers up under the topbar with no scrollbar to ever bring them back. The panel now sizes from its flex parent (which already accounts for the topbar) instead of viewport math, on desktop and mobile both; the compose bar and both headers now fit on screen simultaneously.
- **Channel pills are now per-channel, not protocol-wide.** With two same-protocol companions, the first implementation made every MeshCore channel's pill flip in unison to whichever companion heard the latest MeshCore packet anywhere — all channels suddenly read "433" ("we cant find our channels back"). Each stored message carries the packet_id it came from, so a channel's pill now comes from joining its latest received message back to that packet's actual capture source (`NodeRepository.get_capture_sources_for_broadcasts()`); the protocol-wide lookup remains only as a fallback for channels with no received messages yet. New `scripts/backfill_meshcore_capture_labels.py` (dry-run by default) relabels pre-fix bare `meshcore_usb` packet rows using each companion's own frequency band, learned from the already-labeled rows rather than hardcoded — verified on a production DB copy (2142 rows relabeled, every channel pill then showing its true band).
- **Topbar chip row didn't wrap on narrow (mobile) screens.** A second MeshCore companion (or Meshtastic USB stick) chip could run off the edge of the screen and never be visible at all — `.topbar__group`, the wrapper around same-protocol chips, was `inline-flex` with no `flex-wrap`, so chips that didn't fit on one line overflowed instead of dropping to a new line. Added `flex-wrap: wrap`.
- **Concentrator Meshtastic TX was RF-invisible to every Meshtastic radio — wrong LoRa sync word on transmit.** Reception has always worked (the service-channel demodulator is programmed to Meshtastic's 0x2B sync word at startup), but that fix only touches RX registers: the TX modulator is programmed per-send inside the stock HAL's `lgw_send()`, which only knows LoRaWAN public 0x34 (our board config, needed for LoRaWAN reception on the multi-SF channels) or private 0x12 — 0x2B does not exist on the TX side at all. So every dashboard message, nodeinfo, ACK, or telemetry sent via the concentrator was transmitted with the LoRaWAN sync word and silently discarded by every Meshtastic radio's demodulator; "sent" in the UI, nothing on the mesh. Found live-debugging "tag to Meshpoint works, Meshpoint to tag never arrives" after everything else (channel hash, PSK, frequency, SF/BW, AES) checked out as correct in the TX logs. An earlier `patch_hal.sh` had already tried to fix this by snapshotting TX peaks inside `sx1302_lora_syncword()` — but that function is only ever called by `lgw_start()` with the board's `lorawan_public` flag, so once `lorawan_public=True` became the default for LoRaWAN capture, the snapshot was always 0x34 and the patch silently did nothing (the RX 0x2B fix bypasses that function entirely with direct register writes). `patch_hal.sh` now injects an explicit exported `sx1302_set_tx_syncword()` override applied to SF7-SF12 transmissions (SF5/SF6 keep the fixed 0x12 their fine-sync path requires), restoring the stock source from git first when the old patch is present; the Python wrapper sets it to the same sync word as RX at startup, and `post_update.sh` re-patches automatically on the next update (or run `sudo /opt/meshpoint/scripts/patch_hal.sh` manually). On a `libloragw.so` built without the new symbol the service logs a loud warning that concentrator TX stays Meshtastic-deaf instead of crashing. The vendored reference copy (`extra/sx1302_hal`) carries the same patch.
- **CI test suite fixed after a real regression shipped unnoticed.** GitHub Actions caught 11 failures across the companion-name reapply, rename route, and serial-enrichment tests — earlier per-companion refactoring this release (rename/reapply, per-entry companion names) had changed function signatures and where names get persisted, but the corresponding `tests/` files were only ever checked with ad-hoc stub scripts, not the real pytest suite CI runs. Test fixtures updated to match the new `_reapply_companion_name(source, config, is_primary)` signature and the new per-entry `capture.meshcore_usb[i].companion_name` persistence location; full suite now verified locally (1166 passed) before shipping, closing the gap that let this slip through.

#### RTL-SDR web listener (Radio tab)

- **Browser radio via RTL-SDR dongle.** `rtl_fm` → ffmpeg MP3 streaming with WFM/NFM/AM/USB/LSB modes, tune-anywhere, squelch/gain/level controls, 10-minute idle auto-stop; `GET/POST /api/listener/*` endpoints behind the session cookie.
- **RDS on broadcast FM.** Wideband MPX pipeline teed to redsea: station name, RadioText, programme type, and a BLER signal-quality pill; EU 50 µs de-emphasis reconstruction.
- **Two radio faces.** Digital skin (VFD-style frequency readout, segmented VU) and Analogue skin (slide-rule dial with band scales, preset flags, swinging-needle VU); choice persists per browser.
- **Preset stations.** Favorites with pinning, category tabs, and search across Amsterdam FM, PMR446, marine VHF/UHF, Schiphol airband (true 8.33 kHz carriers), and ham presets; now-playing markers on tab and row. Preset display switched from a wrapped chip grid to a list of rows (star, name, frequency) matching the DAB+ tab's station-list look, once that tab established the pattern -- same category tabs and click-to-tune behavior, just restyled; the frequency is now visible directly on each row instead of only appearing after tuning.
- **Real-time VU meter.** Client-side Web Audio analyser (instantaneous RMS at ~60 fps with peak hold) instead of server-side loudness polling.
- **Clean retunes.** Stop → settle → start pipeline with retry fixes the "Failed to open rtlsdr device #0" race on fast channel switches.
- **P2000 and Pagers tabs.** Two new tabs alongside Radio, decoding live pager traffic instead of streaming audio: P2000 (Dutch emergency dispatch, FLEX on 169.65 MHz) and Pagers (POCSAG512/1200/2400 on 172.45 MHz), each a fixed `rtl_fm | multimon-ng` pipeline with its own Start/Stop button and a live-scrolling decoded message log (timestamp, protocol, capcode, message text). Since the RTL-SDR dongle can only be tuned to one frequency by one process at a time, only one of Radio/P2000/Pagers can be active at once — starting one while another is running returns a clear error rather than silently stopping it (stop the active one first), and all three tabs now show "busy — in use by X" (with Start/Tune disabled) whenever a sibling tab holds the dongle, instead of a bare "idle" that looked like nothing was using it. New `src/audio/pager_listener.py`, `src/audio/sdr_registry.py` (the shared "who owns the dongle" check), and `GET/POST /api/p2000/*` + `/api/pagers/*` endpoints. **P2000 (FLEX) fixed 2026-07-13**: real FLEX pages were being silently dropped — `_FLEX_RE` was written against a colon/space format guessed from documentation (no RTL-SDR hardware to test against at build time), but real multimon-ng output is pipe-delimited (`FLEX|<timestamp>|<baud>/<level>/<phase>/<cycle>|<frame>|<capcodes>|<kind>|<message>`), confirmed by running the exact pipeline manually in a shell and capturing a real page. The old regex's "recognized protocol, unmatched format, show raw anyway" fallback also only checked for a `FLEX:` prefix, so real pipe-delimited pages fell all the way through to being ignored like a blank line, not even shown raw. Rewritten to match the real format; when a page lists multiple space-separated capcodes (simulcast/alternate addressing) the first is shown in the compact capcode column, with the full line always preserved in `raw`.
- **POCSAG tab.** A fourth tab covering the POCSAG512/1200/2400 decoders on a separate 439.9875 MHz band from the Pagers tab, sharing the same `rtl_fm | multimon-ng` pipeline shape and dongle-exclusivity rules. The message parser was confirmed against real captured multimon-ng output on the Pi (`POCSAG1200: Address: 2041152  Function: 3  Alpha:   Test message<NUL><NUL>`), which also revealed that multimon-ng pads POCSAG alpha text with literal `<NUL>` tokens — now stripped for a clean message display. New `GET/POST /api/pocsag/*` endpoints.
- **Digital/Analogue skin toggle and status pill moved onto the Radio tab's own card.** They previously lived in the page-level header, which meant they kept showing on the P2000/Pagers/POCSAG tabs too even though those tabs have no skin or "on air" concept of their own — cosmetic leftover from before those tabs existed. Fixed a follow-on side effect of that move: the status text (e.g. "busy — in use by P2000") inherited the card header's uppercase/bold styling and looked shouty compared to the same text on the P2000/Pagers/POCSAG tabs — now normal case and weight everywhere. The status dot is also now red while busy (a sibling tab holds the dongle) instead of the same grey as plain idle, keeping green reserved for "this tab is actually on air" — applied consistently across Radio and all three pager tabs.
- **Sidebar shows when the RTL-SDR dongle is in use, from any page.** A green-dot badge on the RTL-SDR nav item names which tab currently holds it (Radio/P2000/Pagers/POCSAG/RTL433), so an operator elsewhere in the dashboard doesn't have to open the Listener page just to check. Polls the existing shared `dongle_owner` status field (same one that powers the "busy — in use by X" text within the Listener page itself) every 5 s; hidden when the dongle is free. New `frontend/sidebar/listener_badge.js`, mirroring the existing NodeInfo TX countdown badge's pattern. Fixed a same-day bug where the badge never appeared at all: its top-level `const POLL_MS` collided with an identically-named constant already declared in `update_check_badge.js` — plain (non-module) `<script>` tags all share one global `let`/`const` scope, so the second declaration threw a page-wide `SyntaxError` that silently killed the whole file before `ListenerBadge` was ever defined. Renamed both of this file's module-level constants to unique names.
- **RTL433 tab.** A fifth tab covering `rtl_433` (weather stations, TPMS, remote sensors, and hundreds of other 433/315/868 MHz OOK/FSK devices) — much broader device coverage than the paging-only P2000/Pagers/POCSAG tabs, since it's a single self-contained process rather than an `rtl_fm | multimon-ng` pipeline. Runs with `-F json` so each decoded event is one JSON object per line (rtl_433's own recommended machine-readable format) instead of its default multi-line human-readable blocks — the decoded field set varies enormously by device model (a temperature sensor and a remote control share almost no fields), so the message log shows the model name plus whatever other fields a given event happens to carry, rather than the fixed protocol/capcode/message columns the pager tabs use. Same dongle-exclusivity rules as the other four tabs. New `src/audio/rtl433_listener.py`, `GET/POST /api/rtl433/*` endpoints. Also runs with `-F log` alongside `-F json`: without it, rtl_433 silently suppresses its own startup/error messages entirely (its own hint: `Use "-F log" if you want any messages, warnings, and errors in the console.`), which meant a real fatal reason (device busy, PLL not locked, etc) never reached the log at all; the exit-code note is also no longer masked when an earlier benign stderr line had already set an error message.
- **Frequency display now shows 4 decimal places everywhere on the Listener page.** The POCSAG tab's "listening on 439.988 MHz" was rounding away real precision — 439.9875 MHz was being rounded to 3 decimals server-side before the frontend ever saw it, silently losing the trailing `5`. Bumped the P2000/Pagers/POCSAG backend rounding to 6 decimals and standardized every frequency readout (Radio's tuner display, and the "listening on X MHz" line on all four decoder tabs) on a fixed 4-decimal format, so POCSAG now correctly reads `439.9875` and every tab is formatted consistently.
- **Mini radio player in the sidebar.** While the Radio/RTL-SDR FM listener is actively tuned, the sidebar's noise-floor block swaps out for a compact player — station name and now-playing RadioText when available (RDS first, falling back to whichever preset you tuned to, then bare frequency + mode when neither is available), plus mute and stop controls — so playback can be checked and stopped from any page without navigating back to the Listener tab. Swaps back to the noise floor automatically the moment playback stops. Scoped to the Radio tab only (P2000/Pagers/POCSAG/RTL433 have no audio to control and already get their own sidebar "in use" badge). Mute toggles the actual `<audio>` element's client-side volume directly — instant, no server round-trip, and a different knob from the Radio page's own Level slider (a server-side pre-encode gain that requires a full retune to change). Extends the existing `SidebarTelemetryRail` module rather than adding a new one, since it already owns this exact visual slot. Long station/RadioText combinations that don't fit the narrow sidebar width marquee-scroll, reusing the exact same `@keyframes lsn-marquee` the Radio page's own scrolling station display already uses. Preset names are now persisted server-side (`RtlListener.station_label`, sent with `POST /api/listener/tune`) instead of living only in the Radio page's own in-memory JS state — so the label now survives a page reload for stations without RDS, and any consumer (the sidebar included) reads it straight off `/api/listener/status` rather than reaching into another module's internals. Fixed a real playback bug the sidebar player exposed: reloading the browser while parked on any page other than Listener (e.g. Dashboard) showed "still playing" with the correct station and a live VU meter — because that's all driven by server-side status polling — while the actual `<audio>` element was silently empty, since it only gets a stream attached via the Listener page's own tune flow, which never ran this session. `ListenerPanel` gained `syncAudioFromStatus()`, called from the sidebar's own always-on poll (unlike the Listener page's poll, which only runs while that route is mounted) to reconnect audio the moment the backend is found running, regardless of which page you're on. The sidebar nav icon is now an antenna instead of a leftover headphones icon from back when this was just the single-purpose Radio/FM tab — a better fit now that 4 of the 5 tabs decode text, not audio.
- **DAB+ tab.** A sixth tab wrapping `welle-cli` (welle.io's DAB/DAB+ decoder, installed automatically by `scripts/install.sh` -- `apt install --no-install-recommends welle.io`, same rationale as the RTL433 tab's apt-installed decoder) for browser playback of Dutch DAB+ multiplexes. Styled to match the Radio tab's Digital skin -- LEDs (ON AIR/TUNING), a big VFD-style channel readout, a scrolling now-playing station/DLS tag with an SNR quality pill, a real-time Web Audio VU meter, and a native `<audio controls>` element -- and positioned right after Radio in the tabbar as the other audio tab (decoders come after). Architecturally different from every other tab: a DAB+ ensemble carries several stations at once, so it's a two-level pick -- choose a channel first, wait for welle-cli to decode the ensemble's station list, then pick a station -- rather than the flat preset list the other tabs use. The channel picker is a sub-tabbar (reusing the same `.lsn-tabbar` look as the outer Radio/DAB+/P2000/... tabs, nested one level deeper): a ★ Favorites tab (shown by default so there's something useful to see immediately), one tab per curated channel preset (`12C`/`11C`/`9C`/`7D`/`8B`, all confirmed live at this antenna via `scripts/dab_channel_scan.py`, labeled by friendly name -- NPO/Commercial/Throwback/MTVNL/NH-Flevo -- rather than the bare channel code, with the code itself in the tab's tooltip), and a Manual tab covering the full 38-channel Band III raster (`5A`-`13F`) for anything else. Clicking a channel tab is a pure view switch with no side effect -- browsing a different channel than the one currently playing shows a Scan prompt ("Stops the current station and retunes to this channel") instead of silently interrupting it, so you can look at another channel's tab without losing what's playing; only pressing Scan (or Rescan, on the already-tuned channel's own tab, to force a fresh decode) actually retunes. Picking a favorite switches to its channel's tab automatically so the played station is actually visible instead of leaving the view stuck on Favorites -- that one action is deliberately still immediate, since choosing a favorite already means "play this now." The Favorites tab itself renders as the same station-list style as a channel tab (star, scrolling channel+station text, Play/Stop) rather than a chip grid, so it reads as just another station list; the star there removes the favorite, and Play/Stop toggles playback in place without needing to jump to that channel's own tab first. ★ favorites (channel + station together, browser-local like the Radio tab's presets) do both steps in one click: picking a favorite on a different channel retunes automatically, then waits for that station's sid to appear in the progressively-decoded list before auto-playing it (giving up after 30 s if it never shows). `DabListener` (`src/audio/dab_listener.py`) spawns `welle-cli -c <channel> -w 7979` as a subprocess and polls its own local `/mux.json` every 2 s for the ensemble label, SNR, and station list (service id, name, DLS text) -- the list only ever grows within a tune, so stations appear as welle-cli decodes them rather than the tab blocking until all are found; data-only services (e.g. TPEG) have no MP3 stream and are filtered out. Playback proxies welle-cli's own `/mp3/<sid>` per station through `GET /api/dab/stream/<sid>` -- a thin per-request pass-through, not the shared fan-out `RtlListener` needs for its single `rtl_fm` pipeline, since welle-cli's own webserver already serves multiple simultaneous clients itself. Same dongle-exclusivity rules as the other five tabs (`sdr_registry` owner `"dab"`), and the sidebar's dongle-in-use badge and mini-player both correctly say "DAB+" (not the raw internal owner name). The sidebar mini-player (previously Radio-only) now covers DAB+ too: since the two share one dongle and only one can ever run, it polls both status endpoints and shows whichever is active; DAB+'s "now playing" text -- unlike Radio's, where tuned frequency IS what's playing -- comes from the DAB+ tab's own in-browser station selection via a `DabPanel.getNowPlaying()`/`stopFromSidebar()` bridge, since welle-cli can serve different browser tabs different stations from the same tuned ensemble. New `src/audio/dab_listener.py`, `GET/POST /api/dab/*` endpoints, `frontend/js/dab_panel.js`. Live-tested end to end on the Pi (real NPO ensemble on `12C`, real stations, favorite auto-tune-and-play, "wow totaly amazed great audio quality sofar"). The channel presets went through a real correction pass against actual scan data (see `scripts/dab_channel_scan.py` below): the originally-planned `9C` label and the `11A` preset were both wrong (`11A` turned out to be a Belgian ensemble, not Dutch), and a since-removed `6C` preset (sourced from a different city's scanner data) decoded nothing at this specific antenna -- the current 5 presets are all confirmed live, with labels naming the actual decoded stations. The VFD readout's big/small hierarchy went through two rounds: first swapped from a plain channel-number display to a friendly ensemble name (curated preset name, falling back to whatever welle-cli decoded), then swapped again to lead with the now-playing station/RadioText instead -- that big VFD space was inherited from the Radio tab's own layout, where it was sized for frequency digits a listener needs to glance at; for DAB+, the station name/RadioText is the equivalent glanceable info, not which channel it happens to be on. The channel + friendly name (e.g. "11C · Commercial") now lives as a small tag directly alongside the SNR/PTY pills (same row, same gap as the pills themselves) instead of pushed out to the far edge of the panel. Fixed a real bug where pressing Stop could leave a stale error message showing in the status line (e.g. "idle — ofdm-processor: SyncOnPhase failed") -- that's routine welle-cli sync-retry chatter, not an actual failure (it appears even during a normal successful lock), so it's now filtered out of `last_error` entirely instead of just being misclassified, and `stop()`/the idle watchdog both clear any leftover `last_error` so a clean stop never shows a leftover message from earlier in the session. Favorites rows now show live RadioText too when that favorite happens to be on the channel currently tuned (same `status.services` data a channel tab's own rows use) -- a favorite only stores `{channel, sid, label}` in localStorage, since RadioText changes constantly and can't be saved statically, so this only applies to whichever favorite matches the live-tuned channel; others still show just the plain label. **Later fix, 2026-07-31**: the big VFD now-playing text showed the generic "select a station below" prompt while a favorite click's channel switch/decode-wait (`_pendingPlay`/`_resolvePendingPlay`) was still in flight -- confusing, since a favorite click already has a specific target station queued, not "nothing chosen yet" (user: "confusing because we clicked a fav not just on the channel list"). `_renderNowPlaying()` now checks for a pending favorite targeting the currently-tuned channel and shows `finding <label>…` instead, falling back to the generic prompt only when nothing at all is queued.
- **ADS-B tab.** An eighth tab wrapping [`dump1090`](https://github.com/MalcolmRobb/dump1090) (built from source by `scripts/install.sh`, `MalcolmRobb/dump1090` -- upstream's Makefile has no `install` target, so the two binaries are copied to `/usr/local/bin` by hand after `make EXTRACFLAGS=-fcommon`; the `-fcommon` flag works around this 2016-era codebase's tentative global definitions -- `Modes`, `tDF`, etc. declared without `extern` in `dump1090.h` -- hitting "multiple definition" link errors under GCC 10+, which defaults to `-fno-common`) for live 1090ES ADS-B aircraft tracking. Positioned right after RTL433 in the tabbar, before DAB+ Config. Unlike the P2000/Pagers/POCSAG/RTL433 tabs' append-only decoded-message log, ADS-B renders as a table keyed by ICAO hex that updates in place each poll -- the same shape dump1090's own bundled `gmap.html` and every other ADS-B web UI use, since "which aircraft are visible right now" is the natural model, not a flood of raw messages. `AdsbListener` (`src/audio/adsb_listener.py`) spawns `dump1090 --net --net-http-port 8081` (port picked to avoid the dashboard's own 8080 and DAB+'s 7979) and polls its embedded webserver's own `/data.json` every 2 s for the full aircraft snapshot (hex, flight, squawk, altitude, speed, track, position, message count, seconds since last heard) -- a successful poll wholesale-replaces the table so aircraft that have gone out of range disappear, while a failed/empty poll leaves the previous table in place rather than blanking the tab for one transient hiccup. Same dongle-exclusivity rules as the other seven tabs (`sdr_registry` owner `"adsb"`). New `GET/POST /api/adsb/*` endpoints, `frontend/js/adsb_panel.js`. Tab has a "Metric units" checkbox next to Start listening, on by default, that passes dump1090's own `--metric` flag (meters/km-h instead of feet/knots) on start; the table's Altitude/Speed column labels follow whichever unit the running process was actually started with. A **Map** button next to Start/Stop opens a modal (new `frontend/js/adsb_map_modal.js`, reusing the `pdm-overlay`/`pdm-modal` shell from the packet detail modal with new wide/flush-body variants) showing the same tracked aircraft live on an OpenStreetMap basemap via Leaflet -- the same CARTO dark tiles and default Netherlands view the Topology tab's node map already uses, so the app has one consistent map style. Each aircraft renders as an SVG arrow rotated to its `track` heading (feather-icons style, matching the sidebar's own stroke-based icon language rather than reusing dump1090's bundled Google-Maps-tied plane marker from `dump1090/public_html/planeObject.js`, referenced from a local, untracked clone of upstream `dump1090` kept at the repo root, not part of this repo's own history); color follows the emergency squawk convention borrowed from that same file (7500 hijack, 7600 radio failure, 7700 general emergency all get distinct colors) and dims contacts unseen for more than 15 s. The modal polls `/api/adsb/status` on its own 2 s timer independent of whether the ADS-B tab itself is mounted, and fits the map bounds to the currently-positioned aircraft the first time any appear. **Two follow-ons, same day, from live use**: the Map button is now disabled until `status.aircraft_count` is nonzero (`adsb_panel.js`'s `_render()`) -- previously it was always clickable and just opened an empty map with nothing to show while idle. And the per-aircraft marker swapped from the rotated navigation-arrow SVG to an actual top-down plane silhouette (`adsb_map_modal.js`'s `_icon()`) -- user: "cant we show planes" -- keeping the same rotate-by-track, squawk-color, and stale-dimming logic, just a different `<path>` in the `L.divIcon` markup.
- **Start listening button now greys out once its own listener is already running**, on every Start/Stop-style Listener tab (P2000, Pagers, POCSAG, RTL433, ADS-B) -- previously it only disabled for `busyOwner` (another tab holding the RTL-SDR dongle), so it stayed clickable while your own tab's listener was already active. Harmless server-side (`start()` was already idempotent, a no-op restart), but a stray extra click did nothing useful. One-line change (`startBtn.disabled = !!status.running || !!busyOwner`) in the shared `pager_panel.js` `_render()` covers all four pager-style tabs at once; `adsb_panel.js` got the identical fix since it doesn't share that base class. Radio and DAB+ deliberately excluded -- those are tune-based, not start/stop, so switching station/channel while already playing is the normal flow, not a double-start to guard against.
- **ADS-B flight detail modal.** Clicking any row in the Aircraft table (new `frontend/js/adsb_flight_modal.js`, reusing the `pdm-overlay`/`pdm-modal` shell) opens a modal with everything known about that aircraft. User asked to "have a look in dump1090 how they did it to get flight data etc" -- checking the actual bundled dump1090 web UI (`dump1090/public_html/planeObject.js`, `script.js`) found it does none of that itself: no registration/type/route/photo lookup anywhere, just three plain outbound links (fr24.com, flightstats.com, flightaware.com) built from the flight number for a human to click manually. Built the enrichment properly instead, from two free, no-auth, CORS-enabled public APIs also used by other open dump1090-derived web UIs (tar1090 etc), called straight from the browser (no new backend endpoint): [hexdb.io](https://hexdb.io)'s `/api/v1/aircraft/{hex}` for registration/type/manufacturer/operator, its `/api/v1/route/icao/{callsign}` for origin-destination ICAO codes (each then resolved to a friendly airport name via `/api/v1/airport/icao/{icao}`), and [planespotters.net](https://www.planespotters.net)'s `/pub/photos/hex/{hex}` for a real photo of the airframe with photographer credit. Live API response shapes were confirmed by hand before writing the parsing code (field names like `RegisteredOwners`/`ICAOTypeCode`/`thumbnail_large` aren't guessable) and the three lookups are independent and best-effort -- a 404 (common for GA/military/older aircraft not in either database) renders as a plain "not found", not an error, and one lookup failing never blocks the other two or the always-available raw ADS-B fields (hex, squawk, altitude, speed, track, position, messages, seen) already shown at the top. Verified end to end against a stubbed DOM + mocked `fetch` matching the real confirmed API responses: happy path (registration/type/operator, resolved origin/destination airport names, photo + credit render correctly), and every not-found/no-data fallback path (unknown hex, blank callsign, empty photo array). **Follow-up, same day**: clicking a plane marker on the Map modal now opens the same flight detail modal (`adsb_map_modal.js`'s marker gained a `click` handler alongside its existing tooltip) -- previously only a table row could open it. Since the flight modal can now open on top of the map modal, both bind their own Escape-to-close listener to `document`; without a fix, one Escape press closed both at once instead of just the top layer. `AdsbFlightModal._onKeyDown` now calls `e.stopImmediatePropagation()` before closing so a lower modal's own listener never fires. Live-verified on the Pi: clicking an Air France HOP EMB-190 (F-HBLI, AFR99ZC) from the map correctly resolved registration/type/manufacturer/operator, the Schiphol→Paris CDG route with both airport names, and a real photo. **Second follow-up, same day**: user hit a case where the lookup itself fully succeeded (registration, route, and photo credit all resolved) but the photo `<img>` still came up as a broken-image glyph -- the hotlinked planespotters.net thumbnail failed to load in that particular browser session even though the metadata request worked. The photo block (`adsb_flight_modal.js`'s new `_photoRow()`) is now built with real DOM nodes instead of an HTML string specifically so an `error` listener can be attached to the `<img>`; on load failure it swaps the broken image out for a plain "Photo failed to load in this browser -- view on planespotters.net" link instead of leaving the glyph on screen. Confirmed working normally on a later aircraft (China Eastern 777, CES772) -- the original failure looks like a one-off CDN hiccup rather than a systemic block, but the graceful fallback now covers it either way. **Third follow-up, same day: flight trails.** User: "how hard woould it be to have trails on the planes... yes sounds good so we see where they go". `adsb_map_modal.js` now keeps an in-memory per-hex position history (`this._trails`, a `Map<hex, [lat,lon][]>`) and draws each aircraft's last ~60 positions (roughly 2 minutes at the modal's 2 s poll rate) as an `L.polyline` in that aircraft's own squawk color, drawn under its marker each render. Deduped (a repeated identical position -- e.g. a contact between real position updates -- isn't pushed again, so a trail doesn't pile up redundant points at one spot) and capped (oldest point shifted out past 60). Trails for aircraft that leave the tracked snapshot entirely are pruned (checked against the full aircraft list, not just the positioned subset, so one that briefly loses its fix mid-flight doesn't get wiped); trails only persist for as long as the modal stays open, reset on close, since the whole Leaflet instance is torn down and rebuilt fresh every time it's reopened. The squawk-color/staleness logic (previously inline in `_icon()`) was pulled out into a shared `_color()` so the trail and the marker always agree on color. Verified with a scripted stub (fake `L.polyline`/`L.marker` recording calls, no real Leaflet needed): a moving aircraft accumulates a growing trail and draws a polyline once it has 2+ points; a stationary one dedupes to a single point and draws no line; an aircraft that drops out of the snapshot has its trail deleted; 100 simulated moving polls confirm the 60-point cap holds (`shift()`s the oldest, never grows past it). **Fourth follow-up, same day: stale contacts now drop off the map.** User: "when will they drop of the map? i dont want a map full og gray planes (last position)" -- checked the actual dump1090 C source (`dump1090/interactive.c`) rather than guess: a contact is only purged from `/data.json` after `MODES_INTERACTIVE_DELETE_TTL` (300s / 5 minutes) of total silence; the existing "seen > 15s = dim gray" rule is purely our own frontend's early visual cue and never removed anything, so a stale ghost could sit at its last known position for up to 5 minutes. The map (not the Aircraft table, which still lists everything dump1090 reports) now stops plotting a contact once it's gone 60s without an update -- chosen to match `MODES_INTERACTIVE_DISPLAY_TTL`, the same threshold dump1090's own bundled interactive display already uses to decide a contact isn't worth showing, rather than picking an arbitrary number. Its trail resets at the same time so a contact that reappears later starts a fresh trail instead of drawing one long "teleport" line across the gap it was hidden for. Verified with the same scripted stub: an aircraft accumulating a 5-point trail while moving disappears from the map entirely (0 markers drawn) the moment its `seen` crosses 60, its trail is confirmed deleted while hidden, and reappearing afterward at a distant position correctly starts a brand-new 1-point trail (no polyline drawn yet, no jump-line to the old track).
- **`scripts/dab_channel_scan.py` now captures each station's DAB SId, not just its name** — closes a real gap in the "stations later" work above: the scan JSON only ever stored bare station-name strings, so favorite/preset playback (`dab_panel.js`'s `_resolvePendingPlay`/`_favMatches`) always fell back to matching by `label.trim().toLowerCase()` once tuned live, with no exact-identity path at all. A DAB SId is broadcaster-assigned as part of the multiplex definition (not a welle-cli session artifact, confirmed via its own `/mux.json`, the same field the *live* dashboard view already reads via `s.sid`), so it's stable across scans and days — unlike a station's broadcast label, which can carry inconsistent padding/spacing that a plain trim+lowercase won't normalize, silently breaking the match with no visible error until the pending-play state's 30s timeout expired (the suspected cause of "favorite click sometimes doesn't start the stream on the first try"). Each `stations` entry is now `{name, sid}` instead of a bare string; `merge_channel_result()`'s union-dedup is sid-keyed when a station has one (falls back to name only for the rare one that doesn't). `dab_panel.js`'s favorite-matching functions (`_favMatches`/`_isFav`/`_favLiveService`/`_favEffectiveSid`/`_toggleFav`/`_playFavorite`) needed no logic changes at all — they were already written sid-aware; the missing piece really was just that the scan script never captured one in the first place. `_presetStationRowHtml()`/`_pendingStationRowHtml()` (the not-yet-tuned preset station list) and `dab_config_panel.js`'s station display both updated for the new per-station shape. Verified: a Python repro against `merge_channel_result()` confirming same-sid re-scans dedup correctly (including when a station's broadcast name drifts between scans but its sid doesn't) and fresh-channel sorting still works: a real V8-context run of the actual extracted rendering functions confirming the real sid lands in both the favorite-star and Play-button data attributes, a station missing a sid falls back cleanly to empty/name-only, and — the core fix, directly reproducing the bug scenario — `_isFav()` now matches correctly by sid even when the live-decoded label text has drifted from the originally-stored one. No migration path needed for already-scanned channels with old bare-string station data: the on-Pi scan-results file was independently wiped for clean testing the same session this landed, so the next scan (full or partial) writes the new shape from a clean slate. **Live-verified against a real welle-cli scan**: a rescan of 5 channels on the Pi produced real sids for all 71 stations, and re-scanning already-known content correctly reported "0 new" across the board — the sid-keyed dedup holds in production, not just in the repro. **A live click-through afterward found the "favorite click sometimes doesn't start" bug still reproduces** — this fix only closes the label-mismatch class of failure (a station present in the live list but missed on a text-mismatch); a slow-to-lock channel (weaker SNR, cold dongle start) can still time out before the station appears in the live list at all, which no identity-matching method fixes. `_resolvePendingPlay()`'s 30s wait window (hardcoded, `dab_panel.js`) is the suspected remaining cause. **Fixed same day**: bumped to 60s and pulled out of two bare literals into a named `_DAB_PENDING_PLAY_TIMEOUT_MS` constant, giving a weak/slow-to-lock channel (cold dongle spin-up + OFDM sync lock + full station-list decode) more realistic headroom before a click gives up. **Live-verified**: user clicked through every channel including 7D and got a station from each one — bug fully closed.
- **DAB+ Config page can now run `scripts/dab_channel_scan.py` itself, with live output** — closes the last remaining CLI-only gap flagged since the DAB+ Config tab first shipped ("Still open: actually triggering a scan run FROM the dashboard"). Same NDJSON-subprocess-streaming pattern as the Meshtastic/MeshCore/POCSAG firmware-flash cards (`window.UpdateStreamClient.postNdjson()` client-side, a duplicated `_stream_subprocess()`/`_ndjson()` pair server-side, matching this repo's existing convention of not cross-importing that helper between otherwise-independent route modules) — user's own framing: "same as the update firmware buttons (sort of) from the companions." New `POST /api/dab/scan/stream`, admin-gated: a **Full scan** button (all 38 channels) plus an advanced picker (checkboxes grouped by band, mirroring `dab_panel.js`'s own `DAB_ALL_CHANNELS` raster) for scanning specific channels, a timeout field (default 60s, matching the live-tuning timeout bumped in the entry above rather than the script's own 30s default), and a "discard existing results" checkbox (confirmed via a themed modal before running, since it's destructive) for the `--new` flag. Only `--channels`/`--timeout`/`--new` are exposed — `--port` (welle-cli's internal webserver port) and `--output` (must always be the fixed path the dashboard itself reads) are deliberately hidden, no reason for either to ever change from the script's own defaults. The real correctness issue this had to solve: the scan script talks to welle-cli directly and knows nothing about `sdr_registry` (its own docstring warns "stop any active Radio/DAB+/... tab first") — bypassing that from the dashboard would let a scan silently collide with a live listener in another browser session. The route now claims the dongle (`sdr_registry.claim("dab_scan")`, a new registry owner name added to every "busy — in use by X" label map alongside `radio`/`p2000`/.../`dab`) before starting and releases it in a `finally` block regardless of success/failure, rejecting cleanly with the same 503 "busy" messaging every other listener tab already shows if something else holds it, instead of a silent USB conflict. A successful scan auto-reloads the channel list below so newly-found content shows up without a manual Refresh. No cancel/stop button (explicit choice — a full 38-channel scan runs to completion, same as the firmware-flash cards have no cancel either). Verified: `tests/test_dab_scan_route.py` (6 cases — busy-rejection leaves the registry untouched, claim/release around both success and failure paths, `--channels`/`--timeout`/`--new` flag construction, timeout-out-of-range validation — subprocess itself mocked, same "not exercised live" scope as this repo's other subprocess-streaming routes, which have no tests of their own), a real V8-context run confirming the 38-checkbox band-grouped picker renders correctly and a no-channels-selected click doesn't fire the request. `node --check`/CSS-brace/`ast.parse` all clean. **Live-verified same day**: user ran a real targeted rescan from the dashboard (`7D 8B 9C 11C 12C`, 90s timeout) and the output streamed correctly end to end (`$ /opt/meshpoint/venv/bin/python .../dab_channel_scan.py --channels 7D 8B 9C 11C 12C --timeout 90.0`, live `FOUND:` lines per channel as they completed). Two same-day follow-ons from that live test: (1) the channel picker now pre-checks this deployment's own 5 confirmed-good NL channels (`7D`/`8B`/`9C`/`11C`/`12C` — the same set the DAB+ tab's original curated presets were built from), so a routine targeted rescan doesn't need re-selecting them by hand every time. (2) The "no scan results yet" empty-state text on both the DAB+ Config page (backend 404 detail in `dab_routes.py`) and the DAB+ tab itself (`dab_panel.js`'s hint) no longer tells the operator to SSH in and run the script manually — DAB+ Config's own message now points at the Full-scan/Scan-specific-channels buttons sitting right above it on the same page, and the DAB+ tab's message points at the DAB+ Config tab by name. **Third same-day follow-on**: the results panel's own standing intro text ("Channels found by `scripts/dab_channel_scan.py`...") also read like CLI-only documentation even after the buttons landed -- now says "Channels found by the scan above." **Fourth**: the output box's own synthetic `# Starting scan -- ...` intro line was removed -- it was modeled on the firmware-flash cards' identical pattern, but unlike theirs (which adds board/port context shown nowhere else), this one just repeated the channels/timeout the very next line -- the real echoed `$ ... --channels ... --timeout ...` command -- already states more precisely; the status line above the output box already covers the at-a-glance summary, so it was redundant with both, not either. Also cleaned up that echoed command's own cosmetic noise: a whole-number timeout now shows as `--timeout 90` instead of `--timeout 90.0` (`str(180.0)`'s trailing `.0` was never meaningful to the script's own `type=float` argument -- `"90"` and `"90.0"` parse identically -- just visual clutter for the common case of typing a plain integer into the seconds field; a genuinely fractional timeout like `45.5` still keeps its decimal). **Fifth**: the per-channel timeout cap was raised from 180s to 240s (both the UI field's `max` and the API's `Field(le=...)` validation) after the user found some slow-to-lock channels still needed multiple scan attempts even at the old ceiling -- the scan script's own `--timeout` has no upper bound of its own, so 180 was purely this dashboard's self-imposed limit, not a real constraint.
- **Clear button on P2000, Pagers, POCSAG, and RTL433.** A Clear button next to Start/Stop on each of these four tabs empties the on-screen decoded-message history without touching whether the listener is running -- previously the only way to get rid of old messages was stopping the listener (which doesn't clear anything either) or reloading the page. Since all four tabs already share one frontend component (`PagerPanel` in `frontend/js/pager_panel.js`) and P2000/Pagers/POCSAG already share one backend class (`PagerListener`) and one route factory (`_add_endpoints()` in `src/api/routes/pager_routes.py`), this needed exactly two backend `clear()` methods (`PagerListener`, `Rtl433Listener`, each just emptying the message deque) and two new `POST /clear` routes (the shared p2000/pagers/pocsag factory, plus `rtl433_routes.py`) to cover all four tabs -- no per-tab duplication. ADS-B intentionally excluded from this pass (different display model -- a live aircraft table, not a message log -- so "clear" means something different there; left for a follow-up).
- **"Hide idle frames" checkbox on P2000, Pagers, POCSAG, and RTL433.** POCSAG batches pad every frame slot not carrying a real page with a fixed idle code word (see the ADS-B/POCSAG test rig work above); multimon-ng doesn't recognize that pattern specially and decodes it like any other address, which shows up as a flood of single-digit `Address: 0`-`7`, `Function: 0` lines with no message text -- confirmed live while testing `extra/pocsag_test/pocsag_test.ino` against the real POCSAG tab, where genuine test pages were buried in dozens of these per second. Real-world POCSAG capcodes are never single digits, so filtering on capcode &lt; 8 + function 0 + no message text is a safe, practical way to hide this structural noise -- new checkbox in the shared `pager_panel.js`, off by default so existing behavior doesn't silently change for anyone not on POCSAG/Pagers, persisted in `localStorage`. Required one small backend addition first: `PagerListener._parse_line()` (`src/audio/pager_listener.py`) was already regex-extracting the `Function:` field from multimon-ng's POCSAG output but discarding it -- now included in the returned message dict so the frontend has something reliable to filter on instead of re-parsing raw text. Naturally a no-op on P2000 (FLEX has no `function` field at all) and RTL433 (free-form JSON events, no capcode/function shape), so sharing the one checkbox across all four tabs needed no per-kind branching.
- **DAB+ Config tab.** A seventh Listener tab, read-only against the RTL-SDR dongle itself (no `sdr_registry` claim -- it never tunes/starts/stops anything), showing every channel `scripts/dab_channel_scan.py` found content on: channel code, ensemble name, SNR, station list, and an editable display-name override layered on top of the raw scanned label without touching it. New `GET /api/dab/scan-results` (viewer-open, matching the rest of `dab_routes.py`'s read endpoints) reads the scan script's JSON output (`config/dab_channel_scan.json`, resolved the same Mac-dev-vs-Pi-install-portable way as `repo_source.py` -- `MESHPOINT_DIR` or cwd) and 404s with a clear message telling the operator to run the scan script first if the file doesn't exist yet; new `PUT /api/dab/scan-results/{channel}/name` (admin-gated, matching every other mutating DAB route) sets or clears (empty string) a `custom_name` field per channel. `scripts/dab_channel_scan.py`'s `merge_channel_result()` was also fixed the same day so a `custom_name` set via this tab survives a later rescan of that channel -- it previously rebuilt each merged entry from only the 5 fields the script itself knows about, which would have silently dropped any web-UI-added field the next time that channel got rescanned; it now starts from a copy of the existing entry so unknown extra fields carry forward. New `frontend/js/dab_config_panel.js`, wired into `listener_panel.js` as an ordinary seventh tab (button, content div, mount, and explicit `_showActiveTab`/`_switchTab` branches -- the tab-dispatch `if/else` chain has no central registry, so a missing branch would have silently fallen through to the Radio tab's status-polling default instead of showing this tab's content). First step of a two-part plan: this tab is the read/edit surface; a later step will make the DAB+ tab itself read its hardcoded channel presets from this same JSON instead. **Second step, same day**: the DAB+ tab's channel picker (`frontend/js/dab_panel.js`) no longer hardcodes `DAB_CHANNEL_PRESETS` -- it now fetches `GET /api/dab/scan-results` once per mount and builds its Favorites/`<scanned channels>`/Manual tabbar from whatever channels were actually found (`custom_name` from the Config tab preferred, else the scanned ensemble label, else the bare channel code), so the tabs match wherever the antenna actually is instead of one location's presets. A missing/unreadable scan-results file just means no channel tabs beyond Favorites/Manual, not an error. The two other places that referenced the old hardcoded array (disabling a channel tab while another tab holds the dongle; the "channel · name" tag shown once tuned) now read from the same fetched list. User explicitly scoped this to channel numbers/names first, stations later. **Also fixed in the same pass**: `NO_LABEL_PLACEHOLDER`'s wording (`scripts/dab_channel_scan.py`) changed from `"{channel} (no name broadcast -- set label in config)"` to a plain `"{channel} (unnamed)"` -- the old text read as an instruction to go edit a config file somewhere, confusing on the very tab that IS the place to set it (the user: "the user will think he has to change something in the config"), and would have made an overly long DAB+ tab button label for any channel with no custom_name set. Verified end to end against the real repaired `config/dab_channel_scan.json`: the real extracted `_chanTabsHtml`/`_loadChannelPresets` logic run in a live V8 context confirms the correct 5 channels load, `custom_name` wins over the raw ensemble label where set, a channel with no override falls back to its scanned label, and a 404 gracefully clears to just Favorites/Manual. **Third step, same day, real bug found live**: fetching scan results only once at `mount()` time (page load) meant the DAB+ tab could get permanently stuck showing zero channel tabs if the file wasn't ready yet at that exact moment -- unlike the Config tab, which re-fetches every time it's opened and so always shows the current truth. `_loadChannelPresets()` is now also called from `show()` (every time the DAB+ tab becomes active), not just `mount()`, so a scan run after the page loaded shows up next time the tab is reopened instead of needing a full page reload. Also added an explicit hint ("No preset channels found — run scripts/dab_channel_scan.py on the device, then reopen this tab.") shown below the channel tabbar whenever there are zero preset channels — covers a missing file, an empty-but-valid one, and a network error, all with the same clear message instead of silently showing just Favorites/Manual with no explanation. Verified against all four cases (channels found, 404, valid file with nothing scanned yet, fetch throwing) via the real extracted logic in a live V8 context. **Fourth step, 2026-07-20, the "stations later" part**: browsing a channel tab that isn't the one currently tuned now lists that channel's known stations straight from the scan JSON (previously just a "Not currently tuned" message and the Scan button, even though the JSON already had every station name) -- each one a Play button that tunes the channel in and auto-plays that exact station once welle-cli decodes it. The scan JSON has no `sid` for a station (welle-cli only hands one out once actually decoding), so this reuses the same wait-and-match mechanism a favorite jump already used (`_pendingPlay`/`_resolvePendingPlay`), extended to match by normalized station name instead of requiring a `sid` up front, then plays the real `sid` once it appears in the live-decoded list. The already-tuned view (full station rows with star/Play-Stop/live DLS) is unchanged; browsing a non-tuned tab is still side-effect-free until Play or Scan is actually clicked. No backend changes needed. Verified via a stubbed-`document` V8 context run: not-tuned render includes a correctly-addressed Play button per known station, presets still render safely while tuned to a *different* channel, and the pending-play name match correctly resolves to the real `sid` once a live scan decodes it. **Fifth step, same day**: two follow-ons from live testing on the Pi. First, favoriting only worked from an already-tuned station row (keyed by `sid`), so the new not-tuned preset list had no star at all -- user: "i see the stations before we could favorite stations". Favorite matching now falls back to a normalized station-name match whenever either side lacks a `sid`, so a favorite added straight from the preset list (stored with `sid: null`) is still recognized once that channel is tuned and the real live row appears, and un-favoriting from either side removes the same entry instead of leaving a duplicate. Second, confirmed (per a user question) that the live station list fully replaces the preset list once tuned rather than merging with it -- which meant the view briefly blanked to "Scanning… stations appear as they decode." the instant a tune started, even though the station names were already known from the last scan. Fixed: that moment now also shows the known names as dimmed, non-interactive placeholder rows, each swapped out for the real clickable one as soon as welle-cli actually decodes it. **Sixth step, same day, real bug caught live**: user reported the new preset-added favorites stopped playing on click. Root cause was a `null === null` false positive -- the Favorites tab's Play handler compared `this._playingSid` (`null` at idle) directly against the favorite's own `sid` (also `null` for one added before ever tuning), so the very first click read as "already playing this, stop it" instead of "not playing yet, start it". Fixed by centralizing the effective-sid lookup so `null` is only ever treated as "not playing," never matched against the idle state, and reused it everywhere a favorite's play state is checked.

#### Roles and access

- **Viewer role fully locked down server-side.** Every write endpoint now requires the admin role: configuration saves (transmit, identity, radio, channels, MeshCore channels), application restart, NodeInfo edit/send, companion rename, and message send/advert/delete. Viewers get a clean 403 instead of silent acceptance.
- **Channel secrets hidden from viewers.** `GET /api/config` no longer returns the Meshtastic channel PSK or MeshCore channel key to viewer sessions; only admins see key material.
- **Admin links stay in place for viewers.** Clicking an admin link inside the app (for example a Hardware-page "Edit …" link into Configuration) no longer navigates away: the viewer stays on the current page and a toast explains that admin access is required. Deep links and fresh loads to admin routes still get the "Admin access required" lock card with a back-to-dashboard link.
- **Blocked sends show a toast.** A viewer using the Messages compose box gets a "Not sent: admin role required" toast instead of a failed message bubble left in the thread.
- **Login page no longer prefills the username.** Both fields start empty on every visit.
- **Role section lists match the real navigation.** The per-role section lists behind `/api/identity` now include the LoRaWAN, Meshtastic, MeshCore, and RTL-SDR listener sections for both roles, so future UI gating on those sections behaves correctly.
- **Upstream's new write endpoints are admin-gated too.** The position and telemetry broadcast-interval PUTs merged from upstream v0.7.7 had no role check; they now require the admin session like every other write endpoint, and CI asserts the gate.
- **SDR start/stop/tune endpoints are now admin-gated too.** A full endpoint audit found the DAB, rtl_433, generic RTL-SDR listener, and P2000/Pagers/POCSAG `start`/`stop`/`tune` routes had no role check beyond the router-level "logged in" floor, so any viewer session could retune the dongle or kill a running decoder. They now require the admin role, matching every other state-changing endpoint in the app; the read-only `status`/`stream` routes on the same listeners stay viewer-open.

#### Hardware page and band spectrum

- **Band spectrum card on the RF Environment page.** The SX1302's spectral scanner now sweeps the whole region band (one scan per 100 kHz, EU868: 863–870 MHz) every 5 minutes and draws the result as a spectrum chart — median and peak (p95) level per step — with the LoRaWAN, Meshtastic, and MeshCore channel positions overlaid as markers. Includes an admin "Sweep now" button and hover readout; sweep cadence is configurable via `radio.spectrum_sweep_interval_seconds` (0 = on-demand only). Packet capture continues during sweeps. While the first sweep is still running the card shows a placeholder and fills in automatically instead of hiding.
- **Spectral-scan percentiles fixed on descending-histogram HALs.** The M1's libloragw returns the spectral-scan histogram with levels in descending order, which flipped the percentile walk — the sweep occasionally reported peak below median, and the noise-floor pill computed its floor from the wrong end of the histogram. Levels are now sorted before the walk, so floor ≤ median ≤ peak always holds.
- **Concentrator channel plan visible on the Hardware page.** A new read-only card lists all 9 SX1302 slots — frequency, bandwidth, SF, sync word, protocol, RF chain, and state per channel (EU868: ch0–ch4 LoRaWAN sniffing at 867.9–868.7 MHz with sync 0x34, ch5–ch7 disabled, ch8 Meshtastic at 869.525 MHz with sync 0x2B) — so the full multi-protocol setup is finally self-explanatory from the dashboard.
- **Hardware page: Meshtastic settings unified in one card.** The "Radio Configuration" card is now "Meshtastic Configuration" and includes a compact channel list (matching the MeshCore card's style); the separate Channels card is gone. The computed values (SF, BW, CR, sync word, preamble) render as regular label/value rows in the same grid as region and frequency instead of a separate tile strip. The MeshCore Companion card top switched to the same label/value rows as the Meshtastic card, and NodeInfo Broadcast moved below the companion card.
- **Configuration → MeshCore Companion card shows firmware version.** A 5th readout tile (Frequency/Bandwidth/SF/TX Power/**Firmware**) reads the companion's own firmware version, with model and build date in a hover tooltip when the companion's firmware reports them. Unlike the other four readouts (a free read of the connect-time `SELF_INFO` handshake), firmware identity needs an actual round-trip to the companion (`send_device_query()`), so it's queried once per connection and cached rather than repeated on every config page load. Response shape varies by companion firmware generation — older firmware only reports a bare protocol-version integer (shown as "protocol v1"), newer firmware also includes a human-readable version string, model, and build date — confirmed against `meshcore-cli`'s own `ver` command implementation rather than guessed, since the `meshcore` Python library's own docs don't describe the payload shape. New `MeshCoreTxClient.get_device_info()`, `GET /api/config`'s `meshcore.device` field.
- **"Check for updates" button next to the firmware readout.** Compares the companion's reported version against the latest `meshcore-dev/MeshCore` GitHub release and shows "Up to date" or "Update available: vX.Y.Z-hash" with a link to the release. Manual/on-demand only — no automatic background polling, since companion firmware only changes when the device is physically reflashed, unlike Meshpoint's own periodic self-update check.
